summary_brief: 2026年5月11日，AI Agent生态进入"Claude Code平台化+企业垂直深化"新阶段。今日最大特征：Anthropic首次以Claude Code为核心构建多代理协作平台（Agent View+Goal命令+Hook系统），标志其从SDK供应商向Agent平台转型；MCP生态则从通用工具集成向支付（MercadoPago）、企业数据（Airtable）垂直行业深度渗透。今日延续了May 9日开启的企业采纳叙事，但推进点是Anthropic自身成为平台层主导者，而非被纳入他人生态。13/23（56.5%）高影响信号比、43活跃仓库、727 commits，均为近期高位，生态在平台竞争维度加速分化。

engineering_signals.title: Claude Code 多代理协作与持久任务执行能力成熟
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Agent View、Goal 命令、Auto-snapshots 等功能共同构建了多代理场景下的会话管理、跨轮次任务执行和状态回滚能力，使 Claude Code 从单代理工具演进为真正的多代理协作平台。

engineering_signals.title: 多代理系统安全加固成为共识需求
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Plan Mode 权限逃逸修复、i18next XSS 边界修复、Ed25519 签名验证三项安全改进表明随着多代理系统复杂度提升，安全边界设计从可选特性变为必选工程标准。

engineering_signals.title: MCP 协议生态快速扩展至支付与企业数据领域
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: MercadoPago（拉美支付）和 Airtable（企业无代码数据库）官方插件加入 Claude 市场，标志 MCP 从通用工具集成迈入垂直行业深度集成阶段，协议成熟度获企业级场景验证。

engineering_signals.title: 可插拔传输架构在多个项目中协同演进
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: gptme 的计算机使用可插拔传输层与 ruvnet/claude-flow 的可插拔共识层采用相似架构思路——从紧耦合单组件演进为 ABC+Interface 双层抽象，体现了 AI Agent 基础设施模块化的行业共识。

engineering_signals.title: Anthropic 多语言 SDK 同步支持 AWS 平台部署
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Python/TypeScript/Go/TypeScript Agent SDK 四条线同步发布 AWS 客户端支持，意味着 Claude Platform on AWS 从预览进入正式可用阶段，多云部署选项成为 SDK 的标准能力。

engineering_signals.title: Playwright 1.60.0 推动浏览器自动化能力边界扩展
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: HAR 录制、拖放模拟、上下文事件订阅等功能的引入，使 Playwright 从网页测试工具扩展为通用浏览器自动化平台，为 AI Agent 的网页交互能力提供底层支撑。

release_signals.title: Claude Code Agent View预览版发布
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增Agent View（Research Preview）提供单一界面查看所有Claude Code会话状态，包括运行中、阻塞和已完成的会话，大幅提升多代理协作场景的管理效率。

release_signals.title: Claude Code Goal命令与跨轮次执行
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增 `/goal` 命令支持设置完成条件，Claude可持续跨轮次工作直到达成目标，配合实时覆盖面板显示进度，大幅增强复杂任务的自动化执行能力。

release_signals.title: Anthropic多语言SDK新增AWS平台支持
release_signals.why_it_matters: Python SDK v0.101.0、TypeScript SDK v0.3.0、Go SDK v1.42.0同步新增AWS客户端支持Claude Platform on AWS，标志着Anthropic正式支持AWS云平台部署。

release_signals.title: Claude Code Hook系统重大升级
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增hook `args`字段支持无shell命令执行，`continueOnBlock`选项允许hook拒绝后继续执行，增强自动化工作流的灵活性和控制能力。

release_signals.title: Playwright v1.60.0重大版本更新
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增HAR录制API、Drop API（模拟拖放）、Aria快照增强、test.abort()等核心功能，并移除多个废弃API，显著提升浏览器自动化测试能力。

release_signals.title: deepagents HITL审批自由文本拒绝理由
release_signals.why_it_matters: Human-in-the-Loop审批流程现在支持自由文本拒绝理由，并增加MCP服务器去重功能，提升企业级AI工作流的人机协作体验。

release_signals.title: Vercel CLI新增Connex服务连接功能
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增 `vercel connex attach` 命令支持将Vercel项目附加到Connex客户端，覆盖多环境配置，简化云服务集成流程。

release_signals.title: opencode Plan Mode安全漏洞修复
release_signals.why_it_matters: 修复Plan Mode中子代理可绕过父代理拒绝规则的安全漏洞，防止权限逃逸，提升多代理系统的安全性。

release_signals.title: Vercel新增Ash框架预设支持
release_signals.why_it_matters: 框架检测器新增Ash Web框架预设支持，扩大Vercel平台对新兴框架的自动适配能力。

release_signals.title: Playwright新增浏览器上下文事件订阅
release_signals.why_it_matters: BrowserContext新增download、frame事件、pageload等生命周期事件订阅能力，增强浏览器自动化的精细控制。

releases.author: ashwin-ant
releases.summary:
## What's changed

- Added agent view (Research Preview): a single list of every Claude Code session — running, blocked on you, or done. Run `claude agents` to get started. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view
- Added `/goal` command: set a completion condition and Claude keeps working across turns until it's met. Works in interactive, `-p`, and Remote Control. Shows live elapsed/turns/tokens as an overlay panel
- Added `/scroll-speed` command to tune mouse wheel scroll speed with a live preview
- Added `claude plugin details <name>` to show a plugin's component inventory and projected per-session token cost
- Added transcript view navigation: `?` for keyboard shortcuts, `{`/`}` to jump between user prompts, `v` to toggle shortcut panel
- Added hook `args: string[]` field (exec form) that spawns the command directly without a shell, so path placeholders never need quoting
- Added hook `continueOnBlock` config option for `PostToolUse` — set to `true` to feed the hook's rejection reason back to Claude and continue the turn
- MCP stdio servers now receive `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in their environment, matching hooks. Plugin configs can reference `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in commands
- Compaction prompt now asks the model to preserve sensitive user instructions
- `/mcp` Reconnect now picks up `.mcp.json` edits without a restart, and shows the HTTP status and URL when reconnecting fails
- `/context all` per-skill token estimates now account for the model's tokenizer and show rounded values
- `claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace>` now auto-refreshes the marketplace and retries before reporting a plugin as not found
- `/plugin` installed-plugin details now show hook event names and MCP server names cleanly
- `/context` now shows the providing plugin's name for plugin-sourced skills
- Remote MCP server reconnect retry on transient failures is now enabled for all users
- API requests from subagents now carry `x-claude-code-agent-id` / `x-claude-code-parent-agent-id` headers, and `claude_code.llm_request` OTEL spans include `agent_id` / `parent_agent_id` attributes
- Remote Control, `/schedule`, claude.ai MCP connectors, and notification preferences are now disabled when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `apiKeyHelper` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is set, even if a Claude.ai login also exists. Unset the API key to use these features
- Fixed a deadlock where expired credentials and the `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` policy setting blocked `claude auth login`/`logout`/`status` with no way to recover
- Fixed `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` not auto-approving commands with shell expansions like `$VAR` and `$(cmd)`
- Fixed a bug where a hook writing to the terminal could corrupt an on-screen interactive prompt; hooks now run without terminal access
- Fixed unbounded memory growth when an HTTP/SSE MCP server streams non-protocol data — response bodies now capped at 16 MB per SSE frame
- Fixed `Skill(name *)` permission rules — the wildcard form now works as a prefix match, matching `Bash(ls *)` behavior
- Fixed settings hot-reload not detecting edits to symlinked `~/.claude/settings.json`
- Fixed plugin details failing to load when the marketplace key differs from the manifest name
- Fixed `/model` picker "Default" row not reflecting `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`/`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` overrides
- Fixed spurious "stream idle timeout" 5 minutes after a response completed, caused by the watchdog timer not being cleared on stream cancellation
- Fixed silent `exit 1` when 10+ MCP servers are configured and the cache directory is unwritable — the error message now includes the underlying cause
- Fixed a typing cursor blinking on tab names, list pointers, and select rows in dialogs
- Fixed transcript view letter shortcuts not working after mouse click
- Fixed Bash-mode up-arrow history repeating the first entry and clobbering the in-progress draft
- Fixed pasting or dropping multiple images only inserting the last one
- Fixed hyperlinks using unreadable dark navy on dark themes — they now adapt to the active theme
- Fixed model picker showing a redundant "Current model" row for third-party users whose model is set to the `opus` alias
- Fixed legacy Opus picker entry on PAYG 3P providers resolving to the same model as the default entry
- Fixed mouse wheel scrolling speed in Cursor and VS Code 1.92–1.104; the trackpad now scrolls at a steady rate and the mouse wheel keeps ~3 lines per notch
- Fixed scroll behavior in Windows Terminal and VS Code when attached to background sessions
- Fixed MCP resources from disconnected servers lingering in `@server:` autocomplete
- Fixed two-file diff snippets over-reporting the number of truncated lines by one
- Fixed Grep results not relativizing Windows drive-letter paths and count mode reporting wrong totals for single-file paths
- Fixed border-embedded text overflowing on CJK/emoji due to visual cell width miscalculation
- Fixed fuzzy-match highlighting splitting emoji and astral-plane characters mid-pair
- Fixed skill argument names containing regex metacharacters breaking argument substitution
- Fixed ProgressBar rendering a full block for an almost-full fractional cell
- Fixed task polling and `fs.watch` being resurrected when the last subscriber leaves while a fetch is in flight
- Fixed plugin dependency resolution leaving a stale count when the manifest name differs from the source identifier
- Fixed Insights Time-of-Day chart skewing when a session has an unparseable timestamp
- Fixed keybindings using only the cmd/super/win modifier being flagged as unparseable
- Fixed `claude_code.active_time.total` OpenTelemetry metric not being emitted in `--print` mode
- Fixed `claude plugin update` not preserving cross-plugin symlinks inside a marketplace
- [VSCode] Press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T to reopen the most recently closed session tab, configurable via `claudeCode.enableReopenClosedSessionShortcut`

key_changes: 新增 Agent View（研究预览版）：通过 `claude agents` 命令查看所有会话状态
新增 `/goal` 命令：设置完成条件，Claude 持续工作直到达成目标，实时显示进度
新增 `claude plugin details` 命令：展示插件组件清单和预估 token 成本
Hook 系统增强：支持 exec 形式的 `args` 字段和 `continueOnBlock` 配置选项
MCP 连接稳定性提升：支持 `.mcp.json` 热重载，远程服务器重连优化
ai_summary.summary_cn: 此版本以新功能为主，包括重磅的 Agent View（会话管理视图）和 /goal 命令（目标驱动的持续工作模式）。同时对 Hook 机制、MCP 服务器连接稳定性和插件系统进行了多项改进，提升了整体使用体验和自动化能力。

key_changes: feat: 新增 content-block-centric streaming (v2)，支持更灵活的内容块流式处理
feat: _format_output 现在支持传递 ToolOutputMixin 实例列表
feat: chat model 和 LLM 调用参数添加到 traceable metadata，增强链路追踪能力
fix: load() 函数加固，抵御不可信的 manifests，提升安全性
fix: batch_size 验证逻辑，防止在 _batch 和 _abatch 中出现无限循环
fix: SSRF 策略修复，恢复云元数据 IPs 和链路本地范围
chore: urllib3、mistune、jupyter-server 等依赖升级，stream_v2/astream_v2 标记为 beta
ai_summary.summary_cn: langchain-core 从 0.3.86 升级到 1.4.0，带来了内容块中心流式处理 v2 新功能，显著增强了流式处理能力。同时修复了多个安全问题（load() 函数加固、SSRF 策略）和潜在的无限循环问题，并改进了 traceable metadata 以更好地支持链路追踪。从 0.3.x 到 1.4.x 的版本跳跃表明这是一个重要的功能版本，但整体保持了向后兼容性。

releases.summary:
## 🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

[tracing.startHar()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start-har) / [tracing.stopHar()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-stop-har) expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same `content`, `mode` and `urlFilter` options as `recordHar`. The returned [Disposable](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-disposable) makes it easy to scope a recording with `await using`:

```js
await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.
```

## 🪝 Drop API

New [locator.drop()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-drop) simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches `dragenter`, `dragover`, and `drop` with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

```js
await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  data: {
    'text/plain': 'hello world',
    'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
  },
});
```

## 🎯 Aria snapshots
- [expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-pageassertions#page-assertions-to-match-aria-snapshot) now works on a [Page](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page), in addition to a [Locator](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator) — equivalent to asserting against `page.locator('body')`.
- New `boxes` option on [locator.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot) / [page.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-aria-snapshot) appends each element's bounding box as `[box=x,y,width,height]`, useful for AI consumption.

## 🛑 test.abort()

New [test.abort()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-abort) aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

```js
test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});
```

## New APIs

### Browser, Context and Page
- Event [browser.on('context')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-event-context) — fired when a new context is created on the browser.
- [BrowserContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext) now mirrors lifecycle events from its pages: [browserContext.on('download')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-download), [browserContext.on('frameattached')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-attached), [browserContext.on('framedetached')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-detached), [browserContext.on('framenavigated')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-navigated), [browserContext.on('pageclose')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-page-close), [browserContext.on('pageload')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-page-load).

### Locators and Assertions
- New option `description` in [page.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-role) / [locator.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-get-by-role) / [frame.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-frame#frame-get-by-role) / [frameLocator.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-framelocator#frame-locator-get-by-role) for matching the [accessible description](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#dfn-accessible-description).
- New option `pseudo` in [expect(locator).toHaveCSS()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-have-css) reads computed styles from `::before` or `::after`.
- New option `style` in [locator.highlight()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-highlight) applies extra inline CSS to the highlight overlay, plus new [page.hideHighlight()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-hide-highlight) to clear all highlights.

### Network
- [webSocketRoute.protocols()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-websocketroute#web-socket-route-protocols) returns the WebSocket subprotocols requested by the page.
- New option `noDefaults` in [browserType.connectOverCDP()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp) disables Playwright's default overrides on the default context (download behavior, focus emulation, media emulation), so attaching to a user's daily-driver browser doesn't disturb its state.

### Errors and Reporting
- New [webError.location()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-weberror#web-error-location) mirrors [consoleMessage.location()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-consolemessage#console-message-location).
- [consoleMessage.location()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-consolemessage#console-message-location) now exposes `line` / `column` properties (`lineNumber` / `columnNumber` are deprecated).
- New [testInfoError.errorContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfoerror#test-info-error-error-context) surfaces additional diagnostic context, such as the aria snapshot of the receiver at the time of an `expect(...)` matcher failure.
- [reporter.onError()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-reporter#reporter-on-error) now receives a `workerInfo` argument with details about the worker for fixture teardown errors.

### Test runner
- New `{testFileBaseName}` token in [testProject.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-snapshot-path-template) — file name without extension.
- Test runner now errors when a config tries to override a non-option fixture, and rejects `workers: 0` or negative values.

## 🛠️ Other improvements
- HTML reporter:
  - `npx playwright show-report` accepts `.zip` files directly — no need to unzip first.
  - Steps that contain attachments inside nested children show an indicator on the parent step.
  - The `repeatEachIndex` is shown in the test header when non-zero.
- Trace Viewer adds a pretty-print toggle for JSON / form request and response bodies in the network details panel.

## Breaking Changes ⚠️
- Removed long-deprecated APIs:
  - `Locator.ariaRef()` — use the standard [locator.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot) pipeline.
  - `handle` option on `BrowserContext.exposeBinding` and `Page.exposeBinding`.
  - `logger` option on `BrowserType.connect` and `BrowserType.connectOverCDP` — use [tracing](https://playwright.dev/docs/trace-viewer) instead.
  - Context options `videosPath` / `videoSize` — use `recordVideo` instead.

## Browser Versions
- Chromium 148.0.7778.96
- Mozilla Firefox 150.0.2
- WebKit 26.4

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:
- Google Chrome 147
- Microsoft Edge 147

## Core

### Improvements

- Added a built-in `customize-opencode` skill so opencode config edits are less likely to break startup.

### Bugfixes

- Fixed numeric HTTP API query parameters in the generated OpenAPI spec and SDK for session and file endpoints.
- Fixed boolean HTTP API query handling so SDK types and runtime validation stay aligned.

- Fixed a Plan Mode security bypass where subagents could ignore parent-agent deny rules.

-   f0d7d32: Disable response streaming for lambdas with `awsLambdaHandler` set inside `getLambdaSupportsStreaming`. This closes a gap where non-Node builders (e.g. `@vercel/redwood`) constructed `NodejsLambda` with `awsLambdaHandler` but no explicit `supportsResponseStreaming`, causing `finalizeLambda` to silently flip streaming on for AWS custom handlers. top_pain_points.topic: Auth re-authentication loop — repeated re-auth required within same long-running task
top_pain_points.summary: Long-running tasks repeatedly enter AUTH_PAUSE state even after successful re-authentication, creating a re-auth loop within a single task. Root causes include token format mismatch, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR precedence override, and missing proactive token refresh in task execution path.
aliases: toolRunner loses defaultHeaders on follow-up calls
top_pain_points.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue that directly impacts long-running task reliability. The loop defeats the core value proposition of the app by repeatedly interrupting task execution with auth prompts. Five concrete root causes identified with file-level precision, and clear acceptance criteria provided. This is not a theoretical concern — the symptom chain (error → classification → AUTH_PAUSE → resume → re-error → re-auth) is fully traced.

source_issues.title: Auth loop in tasks: repeated re-authentication due to token/env precedence and credential parsing drift
source_issues.evidence: Deep-dive report with 5 identified root causes: (1) backend token readers only accept sk-ant-oat01- format while frontend accepts sk-ant-, (2) backend overrides CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with forced token injection defeating config-dir-first behavior, (3) task path lacks proactive token refresh used by usage monitor, (4) credential schema drift between claudeAiOauth and oauthAccount shapes, (5) overly broad auth error classification. The auth loop is fully traced through backend session.py and coder.py. Acceptance criteria explicitly state re-auth should happen once per true credential invalidation, not repeatedly.

source_issues.title: MCP pre-flight HEAD request missing authentication headers

signals.topic: ClickHouse vector database SQL injection via unparameterized delete_by_metadata
signals.summary: The delete_by_metadata method in agno/vectordb/clickhouse/clickhousedb.py directly interpolates user-controlled metadata keys and values into raw ClickHouse SQL DELETE statements using f-strings. An attacker can inject SQL via metadata payload (e.g., {"source": "' OR '1'='1"}) to cause mass deletion of all vector embeddings or extract data via error-based injection.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed PoC demonstrates mass data deletion and information disclosure via SQL tautology injection through unescaped metadata values. While count=1, the severity is critical: arbitrary mass deletion of all vector embeddings and cross-tenant data access in shared deployments. The bug is in a specific database backend (ClickHouse), but the impact (data destruction) is a clear user pain point.

source_issues.title: [Vulnerability] SQL Injection in agno ClickHouse Vector Database via `delete_by_metadata`
source_issues.evidence: PoC confirmed: metadata={"source": "' OR '1'='1"} generates tautology WHERE clause that deletes ALL rows. Before: 3 rows, after: 0. Also leaks secrets from internal rows via error-based injection.

signals.topic: Race condition in parallel tool_hooks leaves run_context.messages permanently stale
signals.summary: FunctionCall._safe_hook_call_async uses a swap-restore pattern on run_context.messages that is not safe under asyncio.gather. When multiple parallel tool calls execute and their hooks are async/await, sibling coroutines interleave swap-restore steps on the shared attribute, leaving rc.messages permanently pointing at a frozen shallow copy. Any subsequent code reading run_context.messages sees stale data.
signals.review_reason: Race condition causes run_context.messages to become permanently stale after any parallel tool call with async hooks, breaking all downstream code that depends on message state (including guardrail hooks, retries, and model inner loop). Although count=1, the bug can silently corrupt agent state in production with no obvious error, making it a significant user pain point.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Parallel tool_hooks race in _safe_hook_call_async leaves run_context.messages permanently stale
source_issues.evidence: Bug manifests deterministically when team/agent emits multiple parallel tool calls with async hooks. Sibling coroutines interleave swap-restore on shared rc.messages attribute. Post-gather code (including guardrail hooks on later iterations) reads frozen snapshot instead of live message list.

signals.topic: Team HITL continuation loses member results and shows stale/resolved requirements

Additionally, resolved team-level requirements reappear as active requirements in subsequent pause payloads, causing clients to re-render old HITL prompts.
signals.review_reason: Clear user workflow breakage: Team HITL continuation is a primary use case for human-in-the-loop agent orchestration. Member tool results being silently replaced by stale delegation placeholders means agents make wrong decisions and users lose control over team member outputs. The bug is deterministic and blocks the entire HITL continue pattern.

signals.topic: SSE event stream race condition — message.part.updated arrives after message.part.delta, causing downstream consumers to drop deltas
signals.summary: On the SSE /event stream, message.part.delta events can arrive before message.part.updated for the same partID due to a fiber scheduling race, causing AI_UIMessageStreamError in downstream integrations.
signals.review_reason: Race condition causes streaming integrations and API consumers to miss text deltas, leading to error states and incomplete message rendering. Root cause is clearly identified in the issue (fire-and-forget fiber vs synchronous fiber publish). This breaks any downstream system consuming the SSE stream reliably.

source_issues.title: message.part.updated arrives after message.part.delta
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: updatePart routes through Database.effect (fire-and-forget on separate fiber) while updatePartDelta publishes directly on the caller's fiber, allowing delta to reach PubSub before update. Downstream consumers receive 'AI_UIMessageStreamError: Received text-delta for missing text part with ID prt_...' because they register part metadata only on message.part.updated.

signals.topic: Panic during SDK client construction when http.DefaultTransport is wrapped by otelhttp (OpenTelemetry distributed tracing)
signals.summary: defaultHTTPClient() performs an unsafe type assertion on http.DefaultTransport, causing a panic when users wrap it with otelhttp.Transport — a standard practice for distributed tracing. This blocks client construction entirely and cannot be avoided even with option.WithHTTPClient(), as the panic occurs before options are applied. Regression introduced in v1.39.0.
aliases: OpenTelemetry integration breaks SDK client construction
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow blocker: the SDK panics (crashes) during client construction when http.DefaultTransport is wrapped by otelhttp.Transport, which is a widely recommended OpenTelemetry distributed tracing pattern. The panic is uncaught and fatal, making the SDK entirely unusable for any application using global otel instrumentation. option.WithHTTPClient() does not help — the panic occurs before caller options are applied. Workarounds require abandoning the global instrumentation pattern, which is a significant degradation for observability-conscious users. Confirmed present in the latest release (v1.41.0) with a clear reproduction case.

source_issues.title: panic: defaultHTTPClient does unsafe type assertion on http.DefaultTransport (breaks otelhttp wrapping)
source_issues.evidence: Panic crashes the application during SDK client construction. Users cannot use OpenTelemetry's global instrumentation pattern (otelhttp.NewTransport wrapping http.DefaultTransport) with the SDK. The panic is uncaught and fatal. Workarounds require abandoning the standard global-otel-instrumentation pattern. Even option.WithHTTPClient() does not prevent the panic because defaultHTTPClient() is called before options are applied. Introduced in v1.39.0, still present in v1.41.0 (latest). No SDK-level escape hatch exists.

signals.review_reason: Confirmed cache visibility race in sequential API calls causes duplicate billing at ~40% rate. Quantified cost impact (3× overcharge on repeated workloads). Reproducible standalone script provided. SDK-agnostic (API-side bug). Blocks cost-sensitive production multi-turn workloads.

Cache_creation_input_tokens billed on both R1 and R2. Sleep 2s workaround eliminates misses entirely. Cost impact quantified for agent workloads (10-100K tokens).

Bug 2: final text block contains mix of invalid JSON + valid JSON + 20+ blank lines. Both bugs prevent reliable structured output in production multi-turn agentic flows.

signals.topic: Server tool results (code_execution, web_search) are silently dropped when client tools interrupt the streaming response
signals.summary: When server-side tools and client tools fire concurrently in the same turn, ServerToolResult blocks are never delivered to the caller after stop_reason=tool_use, causing orphaned tool blocks.
aliases: server tool result missing after tool_use stop
signals.review_reason: Server tool results (code_execution, web_search) silently dropped during concurrent tool execution, leaving orphaned tool blocks. Confirmed in production load test. Causes stuck UI spinners and false failure flags. Affects any application using server-side tools alongside client tools — a common production pattern.

source_issues.title: ServerToolResult not delivered when client tools interrupt the stream (code_execution + client tool concurrency)
source_issues.evidence: Production load test with 5 concurrent users shows orphaned server_tool_use blocks with no matching results. Frontend spinners stuck forever. Monitoring/load tests flag as failures. Workaround requires heuristic cleanup assuming completion at next iteration — unreliable.

signals.topic: toolRunner drops defaultHeaders on follow-up API calls, breaking proxy/gateway authentication
signals.summary: The toolRunner helper does not forward defaultHeaders (and baseURL) on subsequent API calls during the multi-turn tool-use loop. Only the first call includes custom headers. This causes authentication failures when using proxies like Cloudflare AI Gateway that rely on custom headers (cf-aig-authorization) for billing or key injection.
aliases: toolRunner loses defaultHeaders on follow-up calls
signals.review_reason: Main flow is BLOCKED: any multi-turn tool-use loop using toolRunner behind a proxy (including Cloudflare AI Gateway) silently drops auth headers on follow-up calls, causing authentication_error from the API. This is a primary use case for SDK users integrating with proxies/gateways. Confirmed as SDK bug by Cloudflare team. Workaround of manually reimplementing the tool loop is non-trivial.

source_issues.title: `toolRunner` drops `defaultHeaders` on follow-up requests (breaks proxy/gateway setups)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed by Cloudflare team as SDK-side bug (cloudflare/ai#408). Follow-up messages.create calls lose custom auth headers, causing 'authentication_error: x-api-key header is required' from API. Breaks Cloudflare AI Gateway unified billing and BYOK. Workaround requires manually reimplementing tool-use loop.

signals.topic: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking beta.skills.versions.create()
signals.summary: The SDK's multipart form handler always strips directory paths from filenames (stripFilenames=true by default), turning 'my-skill/SKILL.md' into just 'SKILL.md'. This causes beta.skills.versions.create() to fail with '400: SKILL.md file must be exactly in the top-level folder' because the API requires the directory prefix.
aliases: multipart upload strips directory from filename
signals.review_reason: Key workflow is BLOCKED: users cannot create new versions of skills via SDK because the multipart upload handler strips directory paths that the API requires. The API returns a clear 400 error indicating the file is not in the expected location. Users are forced to delete and recreate skills instead of using the versions API, which is a significant workflow regression.

source_issues.title: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking skills.versions.create()
source_issues.evidence: SDK returns 400 error from API: 'SKILL.md file must be exactly in the top-level folder'. Root cause: getName() in internal/uploads.js uses stripPath=true by default. User must use workaround of deleting and recreating skill instead of using versions.create(). Same issue exists in OpenAI Node SDK.

signals.topic: zodOutputFormat helper throws exceptions when used with Zod v3 schemas
signals.summary: The zodOutputFormat helper from @anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/zod throws an error when passed a Zod v3 schema, while Zod v4 schemas work correctly. This breaks structured output workflows for users on the Zod v3 branch.
aliases: zod v3 schema support broken in zodOutputFormat
signals.review_reason: Structured output helper is non-functional for Zod v3 users: the zodOutputFormat helper throws an unhandled exception when schemas from Zod v3 are passed in. Since many projects are still on Zod v3, this breaks the primary SDK helper for structured outputs with Zod integration. The TypeScript typings are also reported as broken for v4.

source_issues.title: zodOutputFormat fails when project uses zod3
source_issues.evidence: Calling zodOutputFormat(Schema3) where Schema3 is a zod v3 object schema throws an exception, while zod v4 schemas pass through without error. Reproducer provided via Stackblitz link.

signals.topic: Streaming responses interrupted mid-transmission without message_stop event for large tool_use JSON payloads
signals.summary: When using streaming with tool_use and large JSON responses (tool output), the stream terminates prematurely without sending message_stop, content_block_stop, or message_delta events. The issue appears to be related to improper backpressure handling, causing partial/incomplete JSON in tool inputs.
signals.review_reason: Streaming is broken for large tool_use responses: streams terminate prematurely without proper termination events, leaving tool inputs incomplete. The user cannot generate comprehensive tool responses because the stream gets cut off around 270-280KB. The issue consistently reproduces and is likely an SDK backpressure/flow control issue as the user suspects. Workaround of slowing stream consumption is impractical for production use.

source_issues.title: Streaming responses consistently interrupted mid-transmission - connection closes without message_stop event
source_issues.evidence: Stream consistently ends mid-transmission at ~270-280KB with 'partial_json':'fa' in last chunk. Error: 'Stream ended without message_stop event'. User spent extensive time debugging with multiple fetch implementations, all yielding same result. Slowing consumption temporarily works, indicating backpressure handling issue.

signals.topic: strict: true causes 500 Internal Server Error with complex nested tool schemas, not a clear 400 validation error
signals.summary: When using strict: true with structured outputs beta and complex nested tool schemas (arrays of objects with required fields), the API returns a 500 Internal Server Error instead of either working correctly or returning a descriptive 400 validation error. This causes long processing delays (~17-55 seconds) before failing with an opaque error.
aliases: strict true complex tool schema internal error
signals.review_reason: Key structured output feature is broken for complex schemas: using strict: true with any non-trivial nested schema causes 500 Internal Server Error after up to 55 seconds of processing, rather than either working or returning a clear validation error. This makes structured outputs with strict mode unusable for any real-world complex tool schemas, which are the primary use case for strict mode. Users lose significant time waiting before getting an opaque failure.

source_issues.title: [BUG] strict: true causes 500 Internal Server Error with complex nested tool schemas
source_issues.evidence: Complex nested schemas with strict:true return 500 after 17-55s of processing. Same schemas without strict:true work fine. The 500 error is opaque (Internal server error) with no indication of whether it's the SDK or API side. Documentation mentions 'Schema is too complex' as a possible 400, but users get 500 instead.

signals.topic: SDK crashes with MessageParseError when thinking block is missing signature field from non-Anthropic-compatible backends
signals.summary: The SDK parser assumes every thinking content block has a 'signature' field. When using non-Anthropic-compatible backends (e.g., gpt-5.4 via compatible API), the backend emits thinking blocks without signature, causing a KeyError crash in the message parser. This blocks the entire query from completing.
signals.review_reason: This is a real runtime crash (MessageParseError) that blocks the entire main query flow. The user explicitly shows the stack trace with KeyError on 'signature' in the message parser, and the issue is reproducible on latest version 0.1.79 with non-Anthropic backends. While count=1, the root cause is a parser assumption violation that can affect any user of compatible backends, making it a P1 rather than P0.

source_issues.title: MessageParseError: missing signature in thinking block with claude-agent-sdk 0.1.79 and Anthropic-compatible backend
source_issues.evidence: SDK raises MessageParseError and crashes the entire query after ~30s when backend emits thinking block without signature. Reproduction: repo URL processing causes failure before any result is returned. Related to #339 (closed not planned) and #473, #786.

signals.topic: Bundled claude binary hangs indefinitely when stdout is not a TTY, affecting CI, Docker, launchd, and orchestrators
signals.summary: The bundled claude binary performs an isatty() check on stdout and hangs when output is piped, redirected, or run in non-TTY environments (CI runners, Docker without -t, cron/launchd, orchestrators). The process goes to sleep state with zero CPU, no output, no error, and must be killed. Combined with RateLimitEvent hanging instead of retrying, this causes silent timeouts in production pipelines.
aliases: TTY detection causes hang in non-interactive environments
silent hang in CI and Docker
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker affecting all non-TTY environments: CI/CD pipelines, Docker containers, cron/launchd jobs, and orchestrators. The hang is silent with no diagnostic output, causing indefinite timeouts (real case: 1800s timeouts for 24+ hours in production). This directly prevents users from running the SDK in the most common production deployment patterns. Strong user impact evidence with a concrete production incident described.

source_issues.title: Bundled `claude` binary hangs when stdout is not a TTY (pipe / file / launchd / cron / Docker)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed 5/5 reproduction: python script hangs when stdout is piped or redirected. Real production impact: launchd-driven nightly pipeline timed out at 1800s every tick for 24+ hours. No error, no output, no progress — only timeout. Workaround requires wrapping in 'script -q /dev/null' which is platform-specific.

signals.topic: stderr callback exception permanently kills the stderr handler loop, dropping all subsequent stderr output
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport._handle_stderr wraps an async for loop in a single except Exception: pass outside the loop. When a user-provided stderr callback raises even once, the loop terminates silently and no further stderr lines are delivered for the rest of the session. Users lose visibility into CLI errors with no indication anything went wrong.
aliases: stderr handler silent failure on callback exception
signals.review_reason: Functional regression: a single buggy stderr callback permanently disables stderr piping for the rest of the session, causing all subsequent CLI errors to be silently dropped. The user has no way to detect this has happened. This directly impacts debugging and observability for production users. The issue includes a reliable 5/5 reproducer and clearly explains the mechanism.

source_issues.title: Bug: stderr callback raise silently kills _handle_stderr loop, dropping all subsequent stderr lines
source_issues.evidence: 5/5 reproduction with mock: second stderr line never reaches the callback after first callback raises. The except Exception: pass is silent — no log, no traceback. Subsequent CLI errors that would reach the user's logger are permanently lost. The 'must not raise' contract is not documented in the stderr: Callable[[str], None] signature.

signals.topic: Subagent session cannot be resumed: agentId hint references non-existent SendMessage tool, causing parent agent failure loop
signals.summary: Long-running subagents truncated by token/turn limits output an agentId hint with instructions to use SendMessage. The SendMessage tool does not exist in the SDK, is not documented, and has no references in source code. The parent agent enters a failure loop calling a non-existent tool, losing the subagent's work. No clean workaround exists.
aliases: SendMessage tool not found subagent resume
signals.review_reason: This causes a failure loop in the parent agent where it repeatedly calls a non-existent tool, resulting in loss of the subagent's completed work (44 tool uses worth). The bug is clearly reproducible for any long-running subagent that gets truncated. It directly blocks the multi-agent workflow pattern, a core SDK use case. The lack of a clean workaround makes this a significant user pain point.

source_issues.title: Bug: Long-running subagent returns agentId with SendMessage hint, but SendMessage tool does not exist
source_issues.evidence: Subagent returns with agentId footer and SendMessage hint; parent agent calls SendMessage -> tool_use_error: No such tool available. Parent enters failure loop, subagent's work (44 tool uses, 315s) is lost. Workaround: subagent must complete all work before session ends, which is not always feasible. 4 comments indicate active user discussion.

signals.topic: ClaudeSDKClient cannot be shared across async runtime contexts due to task group lifetime coupling
signals.summary: ClaudeSDKClient instances are tied to the async context in which connect() was called. The internal anyio task group lives for the connection lifetime and cannot be safely accessed from different asyncio task groups, trio nurseries, or async scopes. This breaks common patterns: sharing a client between workers, reusing a client across task groups, or using the client inside FastAPI/Starlette/etc frameworks.
aliases: task group lifetime blocks structured concurrency use
signals.review_reason: This is a significant architectural limitation that breaks real-world production patterns including FastAPI/Starlette integration, worker pools, and multi-task-group usage. While the SDK nominally works in a simple single-context case, any sophisticated async application architecture is blocked. The issue is labeled 'bug' and the limitation is clearly documented with specific framework incompatibility examples.

source_issues.title: ClaudeSDKClient Cannot Be Shared Across Async Runtime Contexts
source_issues.evidence: Bug filed as affecting v0.0.20+. Client spawns internal anyio task group tied to the caller's async context, preventing cross-context sharing. Explicitly breaks FastAPI/Starlette/Hypercorn-with-Trio integration and worker pool patterns.

signals.topic: Linux musl/glibc binary picker selects wrong variant, causing query() to fail at spawn with misleading ENOENT error
signals.summary: On Linux systems where both glibc and musl variants of the Claude Agent SDK are installed (common with pnpm/npm), the binary picker resolves the musl variant first. Spawning a musl-linked binary on a glibc host fails with ENOENT because the musl dynamic loader is absent. The error message is misleading — it says 'binary not found' even though the file exists. This is a main-flow blocker: query() cannot execute at all.
aliases: musl binary not found on glibc Linux
linux binary picker wrong libc variant
signals.review_reason: count=2 (deduped root cause: same musl/glibc picker bug manifested in 2 reports). Both clearly show main-flow blocker: query() fails at spawn on any Linux system with both variants installed (common with pnpm due to optional dep handling). Workaround requires manually specifying pathToClaudeCodeExecutable. Despite count=2 < 3, the severity is high — this is a startup crash that renders the entire query() flow unusable on Linux, which is a primary target platform.

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: query() fails at spawn with misleading ENOENT; musl binary resolves via require.resolve but cannot execute on glibc host; error says 'Claude Code native binary not found' while file exists on disk

source_issues.title: Binary picker selects musl variant on glibc Linux, causing ENOENT at spawn
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #296; same root cause: musl picked before glibc on glibc Linux; query() fails at spawn with same misleading error

signals.topic: options.hooks causes agent to ignore custom systemPrompt identity, always responds as Claude Code
signals.summary: When any hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SessionEnd) are passed to query(), the agent ignores the custom systemPrompt and responds with the default Claude Code identity on identity-type queries. This affects production multi-agent systems that need custom personas for observability. Even empty handlers trigger it. Workaround (canUseTool) exists but doesn't cover PostToolUse/PreCompact/SessionEnd use cases.
signals.review_reason: count=1 single report, but strong user impact evidence: production 17-agent enterprise system blocked from using hooks (observability) or must choose between identity fidelity and observability. Identity drift is non-blocking for operational tasks but breaks core product value for multi-agent persona systems. P2 due to count=1 and no blocking of main query() flow.

source_issues.title: options.hooks causes agent to ignore custom systemPrompt and identify as "Claude Code"
source_issues.evidence: Custom systemPrompt persona is overridden by hooks option; affects all hook types including SessionEnd (no tool involvement); empty handlers still trigger; production multi-agent system broken — developer spent 8 hours isolating the bug; workaround exists (canUseTool) but doesn't cover PostToolUse/PreCompact/SessionEnd

signals.topic: Internal 'directory mismatch' error causes action failures or confusing log messages on every run
signals.summary: An internal error about 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json' appears on every workflow run for multiple users across different repos. Some users experience exit 1 failures on every run (blocking all use), while others see the action complete but with confusing internal error messages. Affects both SHA-pinned and floating-tag refs.
aliases: Internal error directory mismatch every run
signals.review_reason: Two distinct users across different repos experience action failures or confusing internal errors on every workflow run. Issue 1266 documents complete workflow blockage with exit 1 and a user who abandoned the action entirely. Despite one being marked duplicate, the evidence shows ongoing user impact requiring resolution.

source_issues.title: Internal error: directory mismatch for tsconfig.json
source_issues.evidence: Internal error logged twice during run and again in post-step. Action completes but error is confusing. Duplicate issue.

source_issues.title: Internal error: directory mismatch for '.../claude-code-action/<ref>/tsconfig.json', fd 4 — fails on every run
source_issues.evidence: Separate user (linxdigitalstudio-png) with full reproduction table across 9 runs. Action exits 1 on every triggered run. Ref switching does not fix. User disabled workflow trigger entirely and migrated to cursor-agent as workaround. User granted read access for diagnosis.

signals.topic: v1.0.113 SDK bump breaks all AWS Bedrock workflows with 400 invalid beta flag
signals.summary: Upgrading @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk from 0.2.128 to 0.2.129 in v1.0.113 causes the SDK to send anthropic_beta in the request body instead of the HTTP header when targeting Bedrock endpoints, resulting in immediate 400 errors and complete workflow failure for all AWS Bedrock users. No workaround via CLI flags works because they don't affect the SDK transport layer.
signals.review_reason: Breaking change that blocks ALL AWS Bedrock users from running the action after a routine version upgrade. No action-level workaround exists; users must pin to an older version, creating a maintenance burden. Primary workflow is completely blocked.

source_issues.title: [BUG] v1.0.113 breaks AWS Bedrock: claude-agent-sdk@0.2.129 sends anthropic_beta in request body, causing 400 invalid beta flag
source_issues.evidence: All Bedrock workflows fail immediately with 400 invalid beta flag on first API call after v1.0.113 upgrade. Workaround requires pinning to v1.0.112. Confirmed root cause: SDK sends anthropic_beta in body but Bedrock only accepts it as HTTP header.

signals.topic: claude[bot] self-trigger creates permanent red required checks when addressing its own review comments
signals.summary: The action's anti-loop guard blocks the action when triggered by claude[bot]'s own commit push. This causes a clean actor-policy refusal on subsequent pull_request events, resulting in permanent red required checks on PRs even though the commit is benign and the actual diff has no substantive issue.
signals.review_reason: Prevents PRs from being merged when Claude bot addresses review feedback — a core use case of the action. The loop guard fires on a benign self-trigger, leaving permanent red checks that force manual override. Directly blocks the intended workflow.

source_issues.title: claude-review blocks itself when triggered by claude[bot]'s own commit — permanent red required check on PRs after @claude addresses review
source_issues.evidence: Concrete repo with failing run linked. The PR is left with a failing required check caused by the action's own loop guard on its own bot identity. Forces manual merge decision per affected PR, breaking required-checks-need-green merge policy.

signals.topic: Generated workflow template grants read-only pull-requests permission; action exits 0 on 403, giving false green status
signals.summary: The /install-github-app command generates a workflow template with pull-requests: read instead of write. When the action tries to post review comments, it receives a 403 from the GitHub API but exits 0 (success). The workflow shows green, required checks pass, but the review was never posted anywhere — no feedback loop for users.
signals.review_reason: Users receive no signal that reviews are not being posted. Required checks pass while the core feature (review comment) does not function. This is a silent, misleading success state that wastes CI time and leaves reviewers unaware reviews were never submitted.

source_issues.title: claude-code-review workflow template generates insufficient permissions; action silently swallows write failure
source_issues.evidence: Generated template sets pull-requests: read; review posting requires write. Action exits 0 on 403. Job shows green with no indication review was never written. No feedback loop — reviews silently go nowhere.

signals.topic: Branch name validation rejects commas, failing PRs with comma in head branch name
signals.summary: validateBranchName() uses an allowlist regex that does not include commas, causing the action to reject any PR whose head branch contains a comma. GitHub itself accepts comma-containing branches, and git check-ref-format permits them with no injection risk under the action's execFileSync model. Users with branch names derived from titles, place names, or external system identifiers are silently blocked.
signals.review_reason: Action fails on a legitimate, GitHub-accepted branch naming pattern. Users with branch names derived from external systems or natural language (which often include commas) cannot use the action on those PRs. While frequency may be low, the failure is silent (no indication the branch name is the cause) and blocks the entire workflow.

source_issues.title: `validateBranchName()` in `src/github/operations/branch.ts` rejects branch names containing a comma (`,`)
source_issues.evidence: Action fails immediately with 'Invalid branch name' error before any git operation. Workaround requires renaming the PR branch, which is impractical when branch names are generated from external identifiers. Validation runs before any Claude invocation, making it a pure false-positive.

signals.topic: macOS desktop app: 'Could not load connectors directory' — multiple macOS versions affected
signals.summary: After macOS upgrades (26.5, 15.7.7), the Claude/Cowork desktop app displays 'Could not load connectors directory' on every launch. Confirmed on multiple macOS versions including macOS 26.5 and macOS 15.7.7. Granting Full Disk Access or App Management permissions does not resolve the issue. A related CORS error (#58157) was also triggered by macOS WebKit changes. This is a regression — the app functioned correctly prior to the upgrade.
aliases: Cowork desktop app broken after macOS upgrade
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is completely blocked: the desktop app shows a persistent error on every single launch across multiple macOS versions, and no workaround resolves it. Multiple confirmed users affected. count=2 from explicitly valid issues; a third (#58157, labeled invalid) represents the same macOS WebKit CORS root cause and is listed as supporting evidence.

source_issues.title: [BUG] "Could not load connectors directory" after upgrading to macOS 26.5
source_issues.evidence: Cowork desktop app displays 'Could not load connectors directory' on every launch after upgrading to macOS 26.5. Full Disk Access, App Management, and writable ~/.claude confirmed. Marked as regression related to #42591.

source_issues.title: [BUG] REOPEN: Claude Code Desktop: "Could not load Connectors Directory"
source_issues.evidence: Reopening the connectors directory bug on latest Claude Code 1.6608.2. Yellow error box appears every time the desktop app is opened. No workaround available.

source_issues.title: [BUG] macOS 15.7.7 triggered CORS error
source_issues.evidence: CORS error blocking api/directory/servers fetch after macOS 15.7.7 WebKit update. Same root cause as #58164/#58155 but labeled invalid by triager — included here as supporting evidence of the same regression pattern across macOS versions.

signals.topic: CLI hangs with high CPU usage during execution — lock acquisition failure
signals.summary: Claude Code CLI hangs with high CPU usage. A lock acquisition failure for the version directory was captured in the error log, suggesting multi-process race condition.
signals.review_reason: Main CLI workflow is blocked — the process hangs with high CPU consumption and a lock acquisition failure, indicating a race condition in multi-process scenarios. While count=1, the root cause (multi-process lock contention) is structural and likely affects other users who haven't reported it, making it P0 due to complete execution blocking.

source_issues.title: [Bug] CLI hangs with high CPU usage during execution
source_issues.evidence: CLI keeps hanging with high CPU usage on darwin. Error log shows 'Lock acquisition failed for /Users/martin/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.139' — a multi-process race condition at the version lock level. Feedback ID provided.

signals.topic: VSCode extension: viewport auto-scrolls to bottom on AskUserQuestion / permission prompts, interrupting scrollback
signals.summary: When using the Claude Code VSCode extension, if a user scrolls up to re-read earlier content while the assistant is streaming a long response, the viewport forcefully jumps to the bottom as soon as an interactive prompt (AskUserQuestion or tool permission request) is emitted. This disrupts the reading flow and there is no existing setting to disable this behavior.
aliases: scroll position lost on permission prompt
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation for VSCode extension users: every time an interactive prompt is emitted while the user is reading history, the viewport is forcefully redirected, breaking concentration. No workaround exists. Not P0 because it's a quality-of-life regression rather than a complete workflow block.

source_issues.title: [BUG] VSCode extension: viewport auto-scrolls to bottom on AskUserQuestion / permission prompt, interrupting scrollback
source_issues.evidence: VSCode extension forcibly scrolls to bottom when AskUserQuestion or permission prompt is emitted, interrupting user reading position. useTerminal:true does not mitigate because interactive prompts render in the extension UI layer. No existing setting to disable this behavior.

signals.topic: /voice: second concurrent session fails with misleading 'No audio detected from microphone' error
signals.summary: When /voice is enabled in two concurrent Claude Code sessions on the same machine, the second session fails with a generic 'No audio detected from microphone' error. The first session continues to capture audio normally. The error message misleads users into checking device settings rather than recognizing another session is holding the microphone lock.
signals.review_reason: Multi-session voice users hit a blocking error with a misleading diagnostic message that sends them down the wrong troubleshooting path. The root cause (exclusive microphone lock held by first session) is confirmed, and no path to shared microphone access or a clearer error message exists.

source_issues.title: /voice: second concurrent session fails with "No audio detected from microphone"
source_issues.evidence: Second concurrent /voice session fails with generic 'no audio detected' error. First session captures audio normally. The misleading error message causes users to check device settings instead of identifying the other session as the source of the conflict. Related issues: #30293, #38918, #48450.

signals.topic: Windows: .bat script (apikeyhelper) not terminated on Claude Code exit — orphaned processes
signals.summary: On Windows, when Claude Code spawns a .bat batch file for apikeyhelper and the user exits or hits Ctrl+C, the batch script child process is not terminated and becomes orphaned. This leaves processes running (e.g., HTTP servers, interactive SSO login flows) that must be manually killed via Task Manager.
aliases: Ctrl+C not propagating to child processes
signals.review_reason: Windows users running interactive auth flows via apikeyhelper are left with orphaned processes that hold resources (ports, file handles). The user must manually clean up via Task Manager. This is a recurring issue specific to Windows' lack of automatic signal propagation to child processes, with a full reproduction and root cause analysis provided.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Windows .bat script for apikeyhelper not getting terminated on exit
source_issues.evidence: Windows batch file for apikeyhelper is not terminated when Claude Code exits or receives Ctrl+C. Child process (e.g., Python HTTP server simulating a login flow) continues running, holding ports and resources. Full reproduction steps and test script provided.

signals.topic: Skills introduction notebook lacks prerequisite setup instructions, blocking first-time users
signals.summary: The skills introduction notebook directs users to 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' without mentioning that the GitHub repo must first be cloned, causing new users to hit a blocking error when following the documentation.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed documentation bug (labeled 'bug') where the skills introduction notebook omits a critical prerequisite, causing first-time users to encounter a blocking error when trying to follow the getting-started instructions. While count=1 limits it to P2, it directly prevents users from completing the intended workflow, making it a real onboarding pain point.

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: Users following the skills introduction notebook at platform.claude.com hit a blocking error because the prerequisite step (cloning the GitHub repo) is never mentioned. The notebook instructs 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' with no prior mention of cloning.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin orphaned bun server.ts processes cause CPU exhaustion, ignore SIGTERM, and block new sessions
signals.summary: Three independent reports show orphaned bun processes peg CPU at 100% indefinitely, ignore SIGTERM, accumulate over days, causing sustained CPU draw and blocking new Telegram sessions.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: orphaned processes cause CPU exhaustion (significant cost impact via power drain and system slowdown), make the Telegram plugin completely unusable, and block new sessions from establishing connections. Three independent reports confirm the same root cause across different failure modes.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin v0.0.6: orphaned bun server.ts processes peg CPU 100%, ignore SIGTERM, accumulate indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: Orphaned bun processes peg CPU at 100% indefinitely, ignore SIGTERM, accumulate over days/weeks causing 200% sustained CPU draw and 30-40W power drain on Apple Silicon

source_issues.title: telegram: stuck event loop in old bun server.ts survives SIGTERM, holds Telegram polling slot, breaks new sessions
source_issues.evidence: Synchronous busy loop makes process unkillable via SIGTERM, keeps holding Telegram bot getUpdates slot indefinitely causing 409 conflicts and MCP disconnects for new sessions

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: orphan watchdog false-positive kills MCP on Windows during idle
source_issues.evidence: Orphan watchdog false-positive on Windows kills MCP during idle, session Telegram tools disappear, polling stops, requires full session restart to recover

signals.topic: hookify UserPromptSubmit rules with field: user_prompt never fire due to wrong payload key (prompt vs user_prompt)
signals.summary: Three issues show hookify's _extract_field reads input_data.get('user_prompt') but Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit hook payload uses 'prompt'. Rules silently never fire. Additionally, action: block does not actually block prompts.
signals.review_reason: Critical hookify functionality is completely broken. Users who write UserPromptSubmit rules (a core extensibility feature) see their rules silently fail to match or block. The combination of wrong field name AND broken blocking action means users cannot intercept or control prompts via hookify at all — a fundamental feature failure for power users who rely on this extensibility.

source_issues.title: hookify: UserPromptSubmit rules with field: user_prompt never fire (wrong payload key)
source_issues.evidence: _extract_field in rule_engine.py reads input_data.get('user_prompt') but Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit hook payload uses key 'prompt'. Rules silently never fire, no error, no log line.

source_issues.title: hookify: prompt rules never match — field name mismatch with UserPromptSubmit hook input
source_issues.evidence: Documentation says to use 'field: user_prompt' but actual UserPromptSubmit payload has 'prompt' field. Every prompt rule returns empty string and never matches.

source_issues.title: hookify: action: block does not block UserPromptSubmit prompts
source_issues.evidence: Rules with action: block and event: prompt display their message but don't actually block - Claude proceeds to process the prompt anyway. Response missing 'decision: block' for UserPromptSubmit events.

signals.topic: Telegram channel poller silently dies after MCP health check, breaking incoming message delivery with no error shown
signals.summary: Running 'claude mcp list' spawns a fresh bun server.ts that SIGTERMs the existing poller, takes over polling, then exits. Long-running session never notified its MCP child died. Incoming messages silently stop. 'claude mcp list' falsely reports plugin as connected.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: This is a silent failure of the core Telegram messaging workflow. Users receive no indication that incoming messages have stopped working, and 'claude mcp list' falsely reports everything is fine. This completely breaks the bidirectional messaging use case with no visible error, forcing users to manually restart sessions to recover.

source_issues.title: Telegram channel poller silently dies after claude mcp list / mcp health check from another session
source_issues.evidence: Running 'claude mcp list' or '/mcp' health check spawns a fresh bun server.ts that SIGTERMs the existing poller, takes over polling, then exits. Long-running session never notified its MCP child died. Incoming Telegram messages silently stop. 'claude mcp list' reports plugin as connected because the check itself spawns a fresh poller, masking the broken state.

signals.topic: remember plugin auto-save never saves session files because PROJECT_DIR resolves to plugin install directory
signals.summary: save-session.sh resolves PROJECT_DIR to plugin cache dir (~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/remember) instead of user's actual project. SessionStart banner promises auto-save files that are never created.
signals.review_reason: Core feature of remember plugin is completely non-functional. The auto-save feature that users depend on to maintain session context across sessions never works, defeating the entire purpose of the plugin. Users lose continuity of context between sessions with no indication of why.

source_issues.title: remember: save-session.sh resolves PROJECT_DIR to plugin install dir, never to the user's project
source_issues.evidence: save-session.sh line 57 resolves PROJECT_DIR to plugin cache dir (~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/remember) instead of $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. SessionStart banner promises auto-save files that are never created. .remember/now.md, today-*.md, recent.md, archive.md, core-memories.md all missing.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin inbound messages silently dropped at client layer while outbound delivery works
signals.summary: Bot polling is healthy (HTTPS ESTABLISHED to Telegram API), typing indicator appears, but mcp.notification never injects the channel block into the conversation. Messages from Telegram to Claude never appear.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure for bidirectional Telegram messaging. Users can send to Telegram but cannot receive replies — the core use case of having a conversation via Telegram is broken. The silent nature (no error shown) makes this especially frustrating as users don't understand why their messages are being ignored.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: inbound (TG→session) silently dropped at client; outbound works
source_issues.evidence: User can send messages from Claude to Telegram (outbound works), but messages from Telegram to Claude never appear in conversation. Bot polling is OK (HTTPS ESTABLISHED to Telegram API), typing indicator appears, but mcp.notification never injects the channel block into the conversation.

signals.topic: setup.sh script fails on Windows due to incorrect virtual environment activation path
signals.summary: The `setup.sh` script hardcodes `.venv/bin/activate` (Linux/macOS path) and does not support Windows `.venv/Scripts/activate`, causing the script to fail immediately with 'No such file or directory' error on Windows machines. This is a primary flow blocker for Windows users trying to set up the project.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary flow blocker: the setup script fails entirely on Windows, producing a 'No such file or directory' error at the point of virtual environment activation. This directly prevents Windows users from initializing the project environment, meeting the threshold for workflow runtime failure. The issue includes explicit reproduction steps and error output, and is labeled 'bug' by maintainers.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent Virtual Environment Activation Path for Windows in `setup.sh` Script
source_issues.evidence: Script fails with `./setup.sh: line 18: .venv/bin/activate: No such file or directory` on Windows. Issue is open and recently active with 2 comments, labeled as 'bug' and 'windows'. Author reproduced the exact failure path.

signals.topic: xlsx recalc.py crashes on Windows due to unguarded socket.AF_UNIX attribute access
signals.summary: On Windows Python builds where socket.AF_UNIX is unavailable as an attribute, _needs_shim() raises uncaught AttributeError, causing recalc.py to crash before any LibreOffice work begins. The xlsx skill's core formula recalculation functionality is completely unusable on affected Windows environments.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow runtime crash that blocks the xlsx skill's core formula recalculation feature on Windows. The bug is clearly reproducible with a full stack trace showing AttributeError not caught by the existing except clause. The feature is completely non-functional on affected Windows environments; no workaround within the skill is available (only a manual LibreOffice CLI workaround).

source_issues.title: xlsx recalc.py crashes on Windows: unguarded socket.AF_UNIX access
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: module 'socket' has no attribute 'AF_UNIX' — recalc.py crashes before any LibreOffice work begins, making xlsx formula recalculation completely unusable on Windows with affected Python builds

signals.topic: npx skills add installs to ~/.agents/skills/ but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills
signals.summary: The npx skills add command installs skills to ~/.agents/skills/, but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills, resulting in installed skills never being loaded or available to users.
signals.review_reason: This causes installed skills to never be available to users, making the install workflow entirely broken. While a workaround (manual moving of files) exists, the core user journey is blocked — users following the documented install process end up with non-functional skills.

source_issues.title: npx skills add may install skills to ~/.agents/skills/, but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills
source_issues.evidence: Skills installed via npx skills add end up in ~/.agents/skills/ but Claude Code exclusively scans ~/.claude/skills — installed skills are never loaded, completely defeating the purpose of the install command

signals.topic: run_eval.py never triggers skills with claude -p (0% trigger rate across all queries)
signals.summary: The skill evaluation framework run_eval.py produces a 0% skill trigger rate across all test queries including explicit invocation requests. This makes the entire eval infrastructure unreliable for assessing skill quality and correctness.
signals.review_reason: This breaks the skill evaluation workflow entirely — the eval framework cannot measure whether skills are triggered correctly, making it impossible to assess skill quality. While it's an internal tool rather than end-user facing, it directly impacts developers' ability to validate skill correctness.

source_issues.title: run_eval.py: claude -p never triggers skills/commands (0% trigger rate across all queries)
source_issues.evidence: Tested with 8 skills and 144 queries — every should-trigger query scored 0/3 triggers, including an explicit 'run /lucas:memory-layer please'. The entire eval pipeline is non-functional and cannot be used to assess skill quality.

signals.topic: node -e corrupts CJK/non-ASCII content in docx generation, causing garbled output
signals.summary: When generating .docx files with Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text, the skill's default node -e inline execution corrupts multi-byte UTF-8 sequences through shell processing, producing garbled or ?-substituted characters in output documents.
signals.review_reason: This causes silent document content corruption — users get .docx files with garbled CJK text without any error signal. While the model eventually self-corrects, the primary failure is data corruption in output documents, which is a significant user-facing issue for any user generating documents with non-ASCII content.

source_issues.title: node -e inline execution tends to corrupt CJK / non-ASCII content
source_issues.evidence: Shell processing of multi-byte UTF-8 strings via node -e corrupts CJK characters in output .docx files. The corruption is silent (no error raised) and the document is created with garbled characters. Model eventually self-corrects but wastes token rounds on a predictable, avoidable failure.

signals.topic: document-skills plugin loads all 17 skills instead of only the 4 declared in marketplace.json
signals.summary: Installing the document-skills plugin loads all 17 skills from the repository instead of filtering to the 4 declared in marketplace.json. This causes namespace pollution and potential unintended code execution.
signals.review_reason: This is a plugin loading bug causing 13 unintended skills to be available, leading to namespace pollution and potential unintended code execution. While it doesn't fully block a specific workflow, it violates the documented plugin contract and exposes users to skills they did not request, which is a trust and safety concern.

source_issues.title: document-skills plugin loads all skills from repo instead of only declared ones in marketplace.json
source_issues.evidence: Installing document-skills (which declares 4 skills in marketplace.json) results in 17 skills being loaded, including unrelated skills from other plugins. The plugin loader does not filter skill directories against the declared skills list.

signals.topic: known_location() hardcodes Iowa for all Gemini variants — Gemini 3.x models silently produce zero tokens on GCP Vertex AI
signals.summary: The known_location() function introduced in #6393 returns Iowa for every Gemini(_), including gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview and gemini-3.1-pro-preview. These models require the global endpoint, not us-central1. No error is surfaced — sessions appear normal but produce zero assistant tokens.
aliases: GCP Vertex AI global endpoint broken for Gemini 3
signals.review_reason: Gemini 3.x 模型静默失败，无任何错误提示但完全不输出 token。两个独立 issue 报告同一回归。gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview 和 gemini-3.1-pro-preview 自 #6393 后一直损坏。工作流完全阻断但静默发生，危害更大。

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: us-central1 endpoint returns 404 for gemini-3.x; global endpoint returns 200. known_location() always returns Iowa so retry never fires. Models silently produce zero tokens with no error surfaced. Both gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview (released Mar 3, 2026) and gemini-3.1-pro-preview (released Feb 19, 2026) affected since #6393.

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #9141 — duplicate report. Same regression from #6393. Models gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview and gemini-3.1-pro-preview broken silently.

signals.topic: Ollama driver sends requests to wrong API endpoint (/v1/chat/completions) — provider configuration completely blocked
signals.summary: The Ollama driver uses the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions path instead of Ollama's native /api/chat endpoint. This causes provider configuration to fail with 404 — users cannot set up Ollama providers at all.
signals.review_reason: 用户完全无法配置 Ollama provider，主流程阻断。虽然 count=1，但影响是致命的（配置失败），review_reason 明确指出阻断证据。

source_issues.title: Ollama driver using /v1/chat/completions instead of /api/chat or /api/generate
source_issues.evidence: Provider configuration wizard completes model listing via /api/tags successfully, but then sends the actual request to /v1/chat/completions causing 404 Resource not found. User cannot complete provider setup. Confirmed on Lemonade Ollama API server (GGUF models).

signals.topic: Gemma-4 models produce garbage tokens or null results via bundled llama-cpp — local inference completely unusable
signals.summary: Gemma-4 GGUF models load successfully but inference produces <unused24> garbage tokens or 'null result from llama cpp' errors. Root cause: bundled llama-cpp-2 v0.1.146 lacks LLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_GEMMA4 support and uses heuristic-only Jinja parsing.
signals.review_reason: 本地推理核心功能完全不可用，用户下载了 21GB 的 Gemma-4 模型但无法正常使用。明确的阻断性 bug，证据包含 DB 查询和与正确版本的对比验证。

source_issues.title: Gemma-4 Chat Template Support Issue
source_issues.evidence: Bundled llama-cpp-2 0.1.146 (crates.io tarball, build ~0) lacks LLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_GEMMA4 and full Jinja support. Gemma-4 models output <unused24> garbage tokens or null results. Verified with local llama.cpp b9073 build that works correctly — confirms bug is in bundled version, not model.

signals.topic: LLM spawns all tool calls concurrently without waiting for completion — process OOM-killed, session destroyed
signals.summary: During vibe coding, the LLM fires dozens of tool calls simultaneously in the same millisecond rather than sequentially. This causes memory exhaustion and Goose process is killed by the OS.
signals.review_reason: 进程被系统 OOM-Kill，整个会话被销毁。虽然是单条 issue，但用户直接损失了进行中的工作，证据包含日志时间戳证明并发调用。

source_issues.title: Many concurrent tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Logs show multiple tool calls starting at identical millisecond timestamps (09:23:04.680247Z, .680248Z, .680249Z...). Process was OOM-killed by OS after memory peaked. User was doing vibe coding and lost entire session. Reproduction on Red Hat Linux, goose v1.33.1.

signals.topic: Session silently hangs after chat-mode intercept — 40+ minutes of no response, subsequent messages silently lost
signals.summary: After Goose's chat mode intercepts a tool call and returns a text summary, the session's reply loop terminates silently. No error shown to user. Subsequent messages are accepted by UI but produce no LLM call for 40+ minutes. One message was visible in UI but never persisted to DB.
signals.review_reason: 会话静默挂起 40+ 分钟，用户消息被 UI 接受但未触发任何 LLM 调用，有用户消息从 DB 丢失的证据。体验严重下降，关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: Session silently hangs after chat-mode response — subsequent user messages receive no response
source_issues.evidence: Session 4 experienced two separate stalls: (1) 40+ minutes of complete silence with zero llmrouter requests after a chat-mode text response; (2) second stall that never recovered. DB shows user message stored in UI but never written to sessions.db. Timeline reconstructed from app logs and DB. Session appeared alive but was dead with no error shown.

signals.topic: Bundle size too large, blocking deployment to Convex functions
signals.summary: The @browserbasehq/stagehand and playwright-core combined bundle exceeds Convex's zipped maximum size limit (51.55 MiB > 42.92 MiB maximum), preventing users from running Stagehand within Convex cloud functions — a core use case is entirely blocked.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断型痛点：用户报告 Stagehand 完整打包后体积（stagehand + playwright-core 合计 51.55 MiB）超出 Convex 云函数上限（42.92 MiB），导致其无法在 Convex 环境中运行。这是明确的部署阻断场景，用户明确表示两类库都必须在同一个函数中，无法通过拆分依赖规避。issue 已被关闭（2026-05-08）但标记为最近活跃，说明问题未真正解决。

source_issues.title: Reduce Bundle Size
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'I cannot run Stagehand within Convex functions as the bundle size is too large. Total module size exceeded the zipped maximum (51.55 MiB > maximum size 42.92 MiB). This occurs when I bundle @browserbasehq/stagehand and playwright-core.' No workaround exists — 'there are no alternatives for smaller playwright or stagehand packages, and I need both in a single function.'

signals.topic: Agent cache 跳过自定义工具调用，导致 replay 时登录凭证等关键操作丢失
signals.summary: Stagehand v3 的 agent 缓存功能不记录也不回放自定义工具（custom_tool），导致包含凭证填充等关键逻辑的自定义工具在 replay 时被静默跳过，登录流程失败，缓存机制形同虚设。
aliases: agent cache custom tool replay broken
signals.review_reason: 核心功能降级型痛点：Agent 缓存是 Stagehand 的关键性能特性，用户依赖它加速 replay。当 custom_tool 在记录阶段被跳过（v3CuaAgentHandler.ts 未调用 recordAgentReplayStep）且回放阶段也被跳过（AgentCache.ts 无 custom_tool 分支）时，依赖自定义工具完成凭证填充的登录流程会在 replay 时静默失败。这不是边缘 bug，而是 cache-aside 模式在自定义工具场景下的系统性缺失，issue 提供了精确到代码行的根因定位。

source_issues.title: Agent cache does not record or replay custom tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Issue provides full root cause analysis in source code. Two bugs: (1) In v3CuaAgentHandler.ts, the custom_tool case returns success without calling recordAgentReplayStep(), unlike other action types. (2) In AgentCache.ts, executeAgentReplayStep() switch has no custom_tool case — falls through to default logger and skips step. User states: 'The cache records button clicks but skips the credential filling, causing login failures during replay.'

signals.topic: Stagehand v3 存储状态持久化全面失效（userDataDir 不创建、storageState() 方法缺失）
signals.summary: Stagehand v3 升级后，所有存储状态持久化机制均不再可用：userDataDir 目录从未被创建（即使手动预建也不写入数据），storageState() 方法从 context/page 对象上移除，导致用户无法在测试运行之间保持登录状态，v2 到 v3 的迁移路径断裂。
