signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断型痛点：Stagehand v3 移除 Playwright 依赖后，userDataDir 和 storageState() 两个关键 API 均失效，用户报告在 init() 前/中/后三个时间点目录都不存在，且 storageState() 抛出 TypeError。这是所有需要跨 session 保持登录态的自动化场景的核心能力缺失，影响范围覆盖所有从 v2 升级的用户。社区有 8 条评论表示关注。Issue 提供了详尽的问题分析、代码复现和临时 workaround（但该 workaround 无法处理 HttpOnly cookie，属于不完整规避）。

source_issues.title: Storage state persistence broken in Stagehand v3 - userDataDir doesn't work, storageState() method missing
source_issues.evidence: Issue contains full reproduction with code: userDataDir directory is never created after init() or close(), storageState() throws 'is not a function' on both stagehand.context and page.context(). Root cause identified: v3 removed Playwright dependency, replacing BrowserContext with a custom context object that lacks these methods. Impact rated High by reporter: 'Authentication state cannot be persisted between test runs, tests must re-authenticate on every run.' Workaround available but manually extracts cookies via document.cookie and misses HttpOnly cookies. 8 comments from community indicating broad impact. Affects all users migrating from v2 to v3.

signals.topic: Tool call execution fails silently — invalid_tool_calls not handled by middleware, causing LLM Error 400 and file writes to silently abort
signals.summary: DanglingToolCallMiddleware only repairs missing tool responses for valid tool_calls but ignores invalid_tool_calls. When the LLM emits a malformed tool call, LangChain stores it on AIMessage.invalid_tool_calls — no ToolMessage is ever produced, and downstream providers return Error 400, silently aborting the main agent loop.
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports all describe tool-call execution silently failing: middleware not handling invalid_tool_calls (2890), JSON-embedding causing write_file aborts (2894), and intermittent 'unexpected type str' errors (2854). All three directly block the main agent execution loop. count=3 meets P0 threshold with clear main-flow阻断 evidence.

source_issues.title: [runtime] DanglingToolCallMiddleware does not handle invalid_tool_calls errors, causing LLM provider Error 400
source_issues.evidence: DanglingToolCallMiddleware does not inspect invalid_tool_calls, leaving message history in provider-invalid state → Error 400 from LLM provider, main loop blocked

source_issues.title: [runtime] Write_file tool is brittle for large Markdown payloads due to JSON argument escaping
source_issues.evidence: Large Markdown content with inline JSON/quotes causes AIMessage.invalid_tool_calls → tool never executes, file not written. Related but separate from issue 2890.

source_issues.title: 工具调用返回报错 unexpected type: <class 'str'>
source_issues.evidence: User-written tool returns str (same format as official tools) but intermittently throws 'unexpected type: <class 'str'>' error — tool execution fails unpredictably, main workflow blocked

signals.topic: Agent data loss after creation — agents auto-disappear or are saved to wrong directory, causing repeated user effort and lost work
signals.summary: Users report that agents repeatedly disappear after creation (rebuilt 7+ times). Additionally, logged-in users who create agents find them saved to the default directory instead of the user's directory, with the frontend showing 'agent was created but could not load' error.
signals.review_reason: Two reports covering the same root cause: agent persistence is broken. Issue 2863 shows agents vanish entirely (user rebuilt 7 times), issue 2862 shows a regression where agents are saved to wrong directory. Combined they represent a data loss pattern that wastes user time and blocks the agent management workflow.

source_issues.title: 创建的智能体总是会自动消失
source_issues.evidence: User reports rebuilding agent 7 times due to repeated auto-disappearance, with visual evidence screenshot attached. Clearly demonstrates UX degradation and wasted user effort.

source_issues.title: [Bug] 用户登录状态下create agent 还是被保存到了 default agents目录下
source_issues.evidence: Regression of previously-fixed issue #2782. Logged-in user creates agent → saved to default/agents → frontend shows 'agent was created but DeerFlow could not load it yet' error. Persistent data misrouting.

signals.topic: Conversation messages lost after Docker container restart — active threads become empty on reload
signals.summary: When Docker containers restart mid-conversation (agent mid-response), re-opening that thread shows an empty chat. Idle conversations load normally. Active conversations permanently lose their in-progress messages.
signals.review_reason: Direct user data loss for active conversations after restart. While count=1 prevents P0, the severity is high (complete message loss for in-progress threads), and the pattern (streaming state not persisted) is a meaningful UX degradation. Evidence is concrete.

source_issues.title: [runtime]Conversation messages not displayed after Docker container restart
source_issues.evidence: Active streaming conversations become empty after container restart; idle conversations load normally. Clear state persistence gap for in-progress conversations — user loses in-flight work.

signals.topic: File upload failure — DOCX document disappears from chat window during Q&A, blocking document analysis workflow
signals.summary: When a user uploads a DOCX document for Q&A, the file disappears from the chat window. The document upload/retrieval flow is broken, preventing the core document analysis use case.
signals.review_reason: Concrete file upload failure blocking the core document Q&A use case. The user's workflow (upload docx → ask questions) is completely blocked. Single report with clear reproduction path, though more evidence would strengthen confidence.

source_issues.title: 上传docx文档问答，对话窗口文件会消失
source_issues.evidence: User uploads DOCX for Q&A → file disappears from conversation window. Core document analysis workflow blocked. Chinese-language user report with clear step-by-step reproduction.

signals.topic: Embedded sync client crashes on async-only config tools (e.g., web_fetch with Jina provider), blocking programmatic use
signals.summary: DeerFlowClient.sync chat/stream methods fail when the model invokes a config-loaded LangChain tool that only provides an async coroutine (e.g., web_fetch with Jina). The embedded sync client path cannot handle async-only tools, causing crashes for programmatic users.
aliases: async-only tool crash in sync client
signals.review_reason: Specific, reproducible crash path for the embedded sync client — a documented use case. Blocks programmatic integration workflows. Clear reproduction with config example. count=1 limits to P1, but user impact is high for the target audience (embedded/API users).

source_issues.title: Embedded DeerFlowClient fails when sync chat invokes async-only config tools
source_issues.evidence: DeerFlowClient.sync methods crash when model calls a config-loaded async-only tool (e.g., Jina web_fetch). Includes full reproduction steps and YAML config. Blocks programmatic embedding use case.

signals.topic: Context silently auto-compacts with setting disabled, causing task memory loss and forced redo
signals.summary: When context window fills up during heavy file read workloads, Cline silently and reversibly reduces context usage even with the auto-compacting feature explicitly disabled. Users lose already-processed information, see the agent forget prior instructions and task history, and are forced to redo work — all without any visible warning or notification.
aliases: context auto-compaction silently reduces context window despite being disabled
context loss due to silent auto-compaction
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: user loses already-generated context, agent forgets task history and user instructions, forcing complete task redo. Explicit setting is ignored — behavior is silent and undetectable without watching the context bar. Cost implication (redo = wasted API calls). Single issue but high severity and clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Cline auto compacts context silently even with autocompacting setting disabled
source_issues.evidence: Context usage bar runs backwards from 90k to 60k with auto-compact disabled; agent forgets prompt and prior task context; user must redo completed work

signals.topic: Agent permanently stuck in Pending state after command failure, requiring full VS Code restart
signals.summary: When a command fails (e.g., truncated command like 'git' → 'it'), the agent enters a permanent 'Pending' state that cannot be cancelled or recovered from. The only workaround is a full quit and reopen of VS Code. No error is surfaced to the agent, no retry occurs, and no skip mechanism works.
aliases: agent stuck in pending state after failed command requiring VS Code restart
pending state not cancellable after command failure
signals.review_reason: Critical workflow blocker: agent becomes permanently unresponsive, blocking the entire task. Only recovery path is full IDE restart. High user impact — work is completely halted with no in-app recovery.

source_issues.title: Agent gets permanently stuck in Pending state after failed command execution, requires VS Code restart
source_issues.evidence: Command corrupted ('git' → 'it') caused 'bash: it: command not found'; agent enters permanent Pending state; cancel button does not work; full VS Code restart required to recover

signals.topic: Streaming response hangs indefinitely on network instability without timeout or retry
signals.summary: StreamChunkCoordinator.startPump() awaits with no timeout. When TCP connections enter a half-open state (socket alive but upstream stops responding), the request silently hangs forever. No timeout fires, no retry is triggered, and the user must manually click Cancel — which aborts the entire task rather than retrying.
aliases: streaming indefinite hang on network instability no timeout
half-open TCP connection causes streaming to hang indefinitely
signals.review_reason: Key functionality blocked: streaming is the primary interaction mode and hangs silently without any error or recovery signal. User loses entire task progress when cancelling, with no retry option. Clear API design issue causing indefinite resource leak.

source_issues.title: Streaming response hangs indefinitely on TCP half-open connections
source_issues.evidence: Pump stays parked on await forever with no timeout; 3x exponential-backoff retry path never triggered; user must manually Cancel which aborts entire task instead of retrying

signals.topic: Chat interface renders gray screen during long-form tasks, blocking all user interaction
signals.summary: During long-form task work, the chat interface occasionally turns completely gray. The extension continues working in the background but the UI is fully unresponsive and provides no visible progress or feedback. No useful error information in logs.
aliases: gray screen UI crash during long conversations
chat interface goes gray during extended task work
signals.review_reason: Critical UI blocking: user loses all visibility into task progress during long-form work. Extension continues running (consuming resources) but provides no feedback. Intermittently reproducible. High-impact experience degradation for the primary use case.

source_issues.title: The VS Code Cline extension occasionally encounters a gray screen in the chat interface
source_issues.evidence: Extension continues working but UI is completely gray with no display; no useful information in logs; user cannot see progress or interact with chat

signals.topic: replace_in_file silently reports success but never persists changes to disk
signals.summary: The replace_in_file tool reports 'The content was successfully saved' but the file on disk is never actually updated. This silent failure wastes API costs (user pays for a task that produces no output) and forces users to discover the issue via workarounds like write_to_file.
aliases: replace_in_file false success report without disk write
file write silently fails without error message
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss: the tool claims success while producing zero output, directly wasting API costs. User has no indication of failure and only discovers it when checking the file manually. Affects the core file-editing workflow.

source_issues.title: replace_in_file が反映されず、書き込まれなかったです
source_issues.evidence: Tool reports 'successfully saved' but read_file and editor confirm file is unchanged across multiple Unity C# files; user forced to use write_to_file workaround; ~$2 cost lost per incident

signals.topic: Autocomplete fails silently or shows no suggestions in VS Code
signals.summary: Code autocomplete fails across multiple scenarios — custom API proxies returning non-standard responses are ignored, OpenRouter extraBodyProperties are not forwarded to providers, and direct LLM server responses are not registered. Result: code suggestion feature is non-functional for affected users.
signals.review_reason: Autocomplete is a core feature. Three separate issues across different providers (OpenRouter, custom proxy, Ollama) all report the same user-facing failure: code suggestions are absent or the feature is completely non-functional. This blocks a primary use case (real-time code completion) and has clear user impact evidence (screenshots, error screenshots, videos). Meets P0 threshold: count>=3, core feature broken, multiple sample links.

signals.topic: Continue extension completely inaccessible to screen reader users (NVDA and Orca)
signals.summary: Continue's chat panel and sidebar lack ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and proper focus management, making the extension unusable for blind developers using NVDA (Windows) or Orca (Linux). Buttons are announced as 'unlabeled', settings panels are non-navigable, and chat history is unreadable.
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (NVDA on Windows, Orca on Linux) both confirm the same root cause: complete absence of accessibility attributes (aria-label, tabindex, focus order, ARIA landmarks). Both reporters are blind developers who state the extension is 'completely inaccessible' and 'not usable'. This is a critical accessibility blocker equivalent to a main-flow breakdown for the affected user segment. Count=2 across two OS variants (Windows, Linux).

signals.topic: Continue extension crashes on startup in JetBrains IDE on macOS (Java heap space OOM)
signals.summary: Uncaught Java heap space exception in JetBrains IDE causes Continue to crash immediately on startup. The crash occurs in kotlinx.coroutines internals triggered from Dispatchers.IO, blocking all use of the extension.
signals.review_reason: Startup crash completely blocks the main flow for JetBrains users on macOS. While count=1, the evidence is unambiguous — full Java stack trace showing OOM in a coroutine, and the crash is at extension initialization. The 'startup' nature makes this P1 rather than P0 due to single-reporter limitation, but the blocking nature is clear.

signals.topic: edit_existing_file in VS Code silently fails — reports success but no file changes are applied
signals.summary: When the AI uses edit_existing_file to modify a file open in VS Code, the chat interface confirms 'File edited successfully' but the actual file content remains unchanged. No error message is shown. Users must manually verify with cat or reopening the file.
signals.review_reason: Users trust the chat confirmation but their files are not modified. This is a misleading workflow state: the AI reports success while the file is unchanged. Leads to wasted developer time, confusion, and potential data integrity issues when users believe edits were saved when they were not. Reported with clear reproduction steps, state=open, and 1 comment indicating it is a known race condition with VS Code file locking.

signals.topic: Text cursor jumps unexpectedly during AI file write operations in VS Code
signals.summary: When Continue is writing a file in response to a user request and the user is simultaneously typing a follow-up question, the text cursor is forcefully moved to the file being written, causing the user's in-progress input to be corrupted or lost.
aliases: cursor moves to file during write
signals.review_reason: Cursor jumping corrupts user input mid-typing, forcing users to stop and re-evaluate what was written. While count=1, the user impact is direct data corruption during active use and the bug is specific and reproducible. The issue clearly describes the scenario where concurrent AI writes and user typing cause focus displacement.

signals.topic: Dual executor architecture (CrewAgentExecutor vs AgentExecutor) silently skips reasoning in production
signals.summary: Two parallel executor classes share responsibility; Agent.kickoff() hard-codes the experimental AgentExecutor, causing the reasoning step to be silently skipped while CrewAgentExecutor users get different behavior — no user-facing warning, divergent test suites, and features that must be landed in two places.
signals.review_reason: Architectural defect confirmed by maintainer-level analysis: production code silently uses experimental executor, causing behavioral divergence (reasoning step skipped). Users receive no warning and get inconsistent behavior depending on entry point. Fixes must be applied in two files simultaneously. Direct user impact: reasoning features silently unavailable in the kickoff() hot path.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Two parallel agent executors (CrewAgentExecutor vs experimental AgentExecutor) cover the same responsibility — pick a winner
source_issues.evidence: Agent.kickoff() hard-codes experimental AgentExecutor; reasoning step silently skipped via 'if self.executor_class is not AgentExecutor'; two divergent test suites; 27 files reference both classes

signals.topic: HITL pre-review silently fails open — automated safeguards bypassed without warning or logging
signals.summary: When @human_feedback(learn=True) lessons are applied in _pre_review_with_lessons, any exception (network, auth, LLM, structured-output) is caught and the original output returned silently. No exception propagates, no log entry is written, and downstream components cannot distinguish pre-reviewed from raw output.
signals.review_reason: A confirmed silent failure path in the human-in-the-loop pre-review: when exceptions occur, automated safeguards are completely bypassed without any warning. This directly defeats the purpose of the HITL safety mechanism. The except block swallows all exceptions and returns unchecked output downstream, with no logging to aid debugging. High-impact workflow integrity issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: HITL pre-review fails open and silently bypasses automated safeguards
source_issues.evidence: except block catches all exceptions, returns original output with no logging, no propagation, and no signal to downstream — pre-review may not have run but caller cannot detect it

signals.topic: OpenAI API key works in isolation but returns 401 inside CrewAI agent execution
signals.summary: Users report that a valid OpenAI API key tested successfully via curl and Python scripts fails with 401 invalid_api_key when the same key is used inside CrewAI's agent kickoff(). Environment variable is not correctly propagated to the runtime context where agents execute.
aliases: API key not propagated to agent runtime
OpenAI auth fails in CrewAI but not in isolation
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: users cannot execute their primary workflow (crew.kickoff()) when using OpenAI API. The key is verified valid in isolation but CrewAI's runtime fails to read/propagate it correctly. Two comments indicate this is not an isolated incident. This is a direct, reproducible block on the core use case.

source_issues.title: [BUG] OpenAI API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI with 401 invalid_api_key
source_issues.evidence: Same key verified via curl and standalone Python script; fails inside CrewAI; repeated auth failures in logs during crew.kickoff(); VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch warning present

signals.topic: crewai uninstallable on Intel Macs — mandatory lancedb dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
signals.summary: lancedb dropped macOS x86_64 wheel builds at version 0.29.2, which crewai declares as a mandatory core dependency. Users on Intel Macs cannot install crewai at all via pip (ResolutionImpossible), even for projects that never use memory features. The dependency is not optional.
aliases: pip install crewai fails on Intel Mac
signals.review_reason: Complete installation block for an entire platform (Intel Macs / macOS x86_64). Users cannot even pip install crewai. This is not a runtime issue but a packaging defect: lancedb is made a mandatory dependency despite having no wheel for this platform, and it is only needed for optional memory features. Affects every Intel Mac user attempting to use the framework, regardless of whether they need memory features.

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: pip install crewai==1.12.2 returns ResolutionImpossible; uv confirms no matching platform tags for macosx_15_0_x86_64; 5 comments indicate community impact; lancedb only needed for memory features which many projects do not use

signals.topic: Documentation code example for flow state persistence produces incorrect results
signals.summary: The official docs code sample for mastering flow state (class-level persistence) runs and produces wrong output — the second run returns 2 instead of the expected 4 (should double the first result). Affects crewAI versions 1.14.1 and 1.12.2, meaning the documentation has been wrong for multiple releases.
signals.review_reason: Verified incorrect output from an official documentation code example: users following the docs get wrong results (2 instead of 4), wasting time debugging a non-issue. This is an experience-degrading documentation defect that misleads users trying to learn and adopt the flow state feature. Multiple versions affected indicates sustained impact.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Wrong code in document
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction confirmed: run official docs code, second result is 2 instead of expected 4; affects both 1.14.1 and 1.12.2; user reproduces on macOS Sonoma Python 3.12

signals.topic: Agent execution failures: malformed tool calls and instruction leaks
signals.summary: The agent produces malformed tool calls (missing required file_path parameter in write_file) and leaks raw internal orchestration instructions into user-facing output during task execution.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct but related agent execution failures: malformed tool calls cause validation errors blocking task completion; internal instruction leaks expose system internals to users; agent fabricates git state and corrupts user files. Combined they represent a pattern of unreliable agent task execution affecting core workflow. Issue 26894 escalated to subscription cancellation, showing severe user impact.

source_issues.title: Malformed `write_file` call and Internal Instruction Leak during User Steering
source_issues.evidence: Agent called write_file omitting the mandatory file_path parameter, causing validation error. Also leaked raw 'Internal instruction: Re-evaluate the active plan...' block into user output.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: Gemini CLI v0.41.2 - unexpected tool call
source_issues.evidence: User gets 'Response stopped due to unexpected tool call' error constantly on latest v0.41.2. Blocks agent from completing tasks.

source_issues.title: I'm done, good bye
source_issues.evidence: Agent fabricated git output, claimed a commit existed before modifying files, then produced a patch that overwrote documentation sections and broke Markdown structure. User explicitly cancelled subscription citing trust failure.

signals.topic: CLI crashes / 404 errors blocking all prompts from executing
signals.summary: The CLI crashes or returns 404/Bad arguments errors on startup or during normal use, completely blocking the main user flow. Reported as both an xsel binary fallback crash causing an unhandled promise rejection, and separate 404 bad arguments errors on Win32.
aliases: CLI crash on xsel binary not found
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure — both issues block the user from using the CLI at all. Issue 26875 produces a CRITICAL unhandled promise rejection crash; issue 26857 prevents any prompts from executing. Both are open bugs with confirmed user impact.

source_issues.title: Bug gemini cli
source_issues.evidence: CLI crashed with unhandled promise rejection: xsel binary not found in bundled SEA environment, then ENAMETOOLONG error. Shows CRITICAL: Unhandled Promise Rejection with full stack trace.

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI is not working returning 404 Bad arguments Errors
source_issues.evidence: CLI returns 404 Bad arguments errors, preventing prompts from working at all. Multiple affected users.

signals.topic: Unauthorized quota/API consumption without user-initiated requests
signals.summary: Quota is consumed automatically (25%→28% recorded) without the user making any API requests, representing direct financial loss for paid tier users.
signals.review_reason: Direct financial harm — paid tier quota consumed without any user action, with visual recording evidence. This is a cost-loss issue, not just a UX problem. Labeled P1 by triagers and the user explicitly reports financial impact. Main flow is not blocked but the financial consequence is severe enough to warrant P0.

source_issues.title: Seriously, DEV TEAM, what is this madness? My quota is being used up automatically without me writing ANYTHING.
source_issues.evidence: User recorded quota jump from 25% to 28% with no user-initiated requests. Explicitly labeled priority/p1 by triagers. Shows video evidence of the automatic quota consumption. User explicitly says 'it's a disgrace' and all other users seem to be ignoring it.

signals.topic: Model capacity 429 errors cause long delays without automatic fallback
signals.summary: When encountering 429 'no capacity' errors, the CLI retries the same unavailable model indefinitely without exponential backoff or falling back to alternative models, causing 10-20 minute stalls.
aliases: No model fallback on capacity errors
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure causing significant time waste (~10-20 minutes per incident). The backoff algorithm is present but lacks both exponential behavior and model fallback logic, causing prolonged unresponsiveness. User impact is clear and quantifiable.

source_issues.title: 429 Model Capacity Issues, No sufficient re-routing
source_issues.evidence: CLI stuck trying the same model (gemini-3-flash-preview) repeatedly on 429 errors, with no exponential backoff and no fallback to alternative models (gemini-3.1-pro, flash-lite). User reports ~10-20 minute stalls. Screenshot evidence attached.

signals.topic: Incorrect quota/daily limit configuration for paid tiers
signals.summary: Google One AI Pro users see their daily usage limit incorrectly set to 200 requests instead of the expected 1,500, preventing normal use of the paid tier.
signals.review_reason: Paying users cannot use their subscribed tier's quota, effectively blocking normal use for a significant portion of the day. The tier recognition works (CLI correctly shows the plan) but the enforced limit is wrong, indicating a configuration/platform bug.

source_issues.title: gemini-cli quota error
source_issues.evidence: User on Google One AI Pro plan sees their daily limit incorrectly set to 200 instead of 1,500 as documented for their tier. Tier is correctly recognized in /about status, but the actual limit enforced is wrong.

signals.topic: TransformersModel 不支持 quantization_config 参数，导致 8bit 量化模型无法正常加载到 GPU
signals.summary: TransformersModel 未将 quantization_config 参数透传给底层 AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained()，导致用户无法通过 BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_8bit=True) 将大模型加载到 GPU 中，主流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: 用户明确报告主流程阻断：BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_8bit=True) 配置无法生效，导致大模型无法加载到 GPU。提供完整环境信息、可复现代码和预期/实际行为对比，属于典型的功能缺失型用户痛点。因仅单仓单条，优先级降为 P1。

source_issues.title: [BUG] quantization_config is not supported in TransformersModel
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在 smolagents 1.10.0 中，TransformersModel 接收 quantization_config 参数但不传递给底层 transformers，导致模型以完整精度加载超出 GPU 显存而崩溃。预期行为是支持 8bit 量化加载，但实际未生效。

signals.topic: Codex 模型在交互式会话中无法正常工作（指令被忽略导致过早停止）
signals.summary: 用户反映在 autoresearch 交互式会话中使用 Codex 时，模型会忽略「never stop」类指令而过早停止生成，不同于 Claude 的正常行为，导致交互式 agent 会话体验严重下降。
aliases: Codex model ignores stop instructions in interactive mode
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 明确描述主流程阻断：Codex 在交互式会话场景下忽略关键指令导致会话过早终止，用户无法正常使用交互式 agent 功能。41 条评论说明这是被社区反复确认的真实问题，而非边缘情况。虽然仅 1 条 issue 不足以触发 P0，但属于明确的主流程阻断类问题，符合 P1 优先级。

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: issue 由 repo owner 本人提交，41 条评论表明社区高度关注。Codex 在交互式会话中忽略 never-stop 指令而过早停止，Claude 则无此问题，直接阻断用户使用 Codex 进行交互式 agent 会话的正常使用。

signals.topic: SkillsMiddleware fails to load skills on first agent turn due to empty list guard
signals.summary: SkillsMiddleware's before_agent guard checks if 'skills_metadata' key exists in state, but PrivateStateAttr initializes it to [] by default. The guard fires on first turn (key exists, value is []), skipping skill loading entirely and showing '(No skills available yet)' even when valid skills exist.
aliases: SkillsMiddleware skips loading on first turn
signals.review_reason: Confirmed main-flow bug. SkillsMiddleware's before_agent guard fires on every first turn for all users due to PrivateStateAttr defaulting skills_metadata to []. The key exists so guard returns None, skills are never loaded. Every user hits '(No skills available yet)' on their first interaction. Three independent reporters confirm this, with full reproduction steps. This is a core agent functionality failure that silently breaks the skills feature on first use.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware skips loading skills on first turn when skills_metadata=[] (PrivateStateAttr default)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with reproduction steps. The guard 'if "skills_metadata" in state' fires on first turn because key exists with empty list. System prompt shows '(No skills available yet)' even though crypto skill exists. Affects all users on every first turn.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware skips loading skills on first turn when skills_metadata=[] (PrivateStateAttr default)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report. Confirms root cause: SkillsMiddleware.before_agent skips when 'skills_metadata' in state, but PrivateStateAttr defaults to []. First turn always skips skill loading.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware skips loading on first turn when skills_metadata=[] (PrivateStateAttr default)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report. Root cause: guard 'if "skills_metadata" in state' fires with empty list from PrivateStateAttr default. Fix: change to 'if "skills_metadata" in state and state["skills_metadata"]'.

signals.topic: SubAgent response_format causes malformed intermediate tool call arguments and HITL failures
signals.summary: When SubAgent.response_format is set, the provider structured-output binding is applied to every model call inside the subagent, not just the final response. This corrupts intermediate tool call arguments — structured fields become null or empty objects — and breaks HITL/approval tools that depend on complete structured payloads.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with clear user impact. SubAgent response_format silently corrupts intermediate tool call payloads — a feature that appears to control final result output actually degrades every intermediate tool call. Users relying on SubAgent for structured results while also using HITL/approval tools will get null/empty structured fields without clear indication why. The same subagent produces correct output without response_format and broken output with it, a deceptive behavioral change. Two duplicate reports with full repro scripts.

source_issues.title: SubAgent response_format affects intermediate tool/HITL calls
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed behavioral regression. With response_format on subagent: 'summary' becomes null instead of {'total': 2}, 'options' becomes [{}, {}] instead of full objects. Same subagent and prompt without response_format produces correct payloads. Root cause: _get_bound_model() binds structured-output kwargs on every subagent call, not just final response.

source_issues.title: SubAgent response_format affects intermediate tool/HITL calls
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate. Full repro with two versions (with/without response_format) showing exact payload difference. Also shows tool schema validation failures due to response_format causing all subagent tools to be rebound with structured-output settings.

signals.topic: MCP pre-flight check sends HEAD request without authentication headers, silently skipping all authenticated servers
signals.summary: The _check_remote_server function in mcp_tools.py sends a HEAD request without passing configured headers from server_config, causing all MCP servers requiring API keys/tokens to fail pre-flight with HTTP 500 and be silently skipped.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed blocking bug. MCP pre-flight sends unauthenticated HEAD requests to all MCP servers, causing all authenticated servers to silently fail and be skipped. This is a complete feature blockage for users with auth-protected MCP servers (common enterprise setup). The error is silent (server skipped with no clear message about auth failure), making diagnosis difficult. Two independent reporters confirm, with full reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: MCP pre-flight HEAD request missing authentication headers
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug. MCP pre-flight check sends HEAD without configured auth headers. Authenticated MCP servers return HTTP 500 and are silently skipped. Impact: all authenticated MCP servers fail pre-flight. Reproduction: configure MCP server with auth headers, run deepagents task, observe 'Server did not become healthy within 60s'.

source_issues.title: MCP pre-flight HEAD request missing authentication headers
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report. Full Python reproduction script provided. Demonstrates HEAD without headers returns 500, HEAD with headers returns 200. Root cause: line 861 in mcp_tools.py calls client.head(url) without passing server_config.get('headers', {}).

signals.topic: Modal sandbox deploy template missing app= parameter causes Sandbox.create to raise InvalidError outside Modal container
signals.summary: The bundler-generated deploy_graph.py calls modal.Sandbox.create(image=image) without app= argument. Modern Modal SDK requires app= when called outside a Modal container, raising InvalidError and blocking the entire deploy flow.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed deploy flow blocker for Modal sandbox users. The bundler-generated template always crashes on first use because modern Modal SDK requires app= parameter outside container. This is a complete deploy failure, not a transient issue. Two independent reports confirm, with verified fix. Downgraded to P1 because count=2 (not >=3) despite strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: [deploy] Modal sandbox template missing app= parameter — Sandbox.create raises InvalidError outside Modal container
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed deploy break. Error: 'Sandboxes require an App when created outside of a Modal container.' Every deploy using modal sandbox provider crashes on first SkillsMiddleware trigger. Root cause: SANDBOX_BLOCK_MODAL template at deploy/templates.py line 151 missing app= argument. CLI's own sandbox_factory.py already handles this correctly, but the deploy template doesn't.

source_issues.title: [deploy] Modal sandbox template missing app= parameter — Sandbox.create raises InvalidError outside Modal container
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report. Same root cause: deploy template forgot to mirror the app= handling from CLI's sandbox_factory. Verified fix locally — applying the patch makes bundler-generated deploy_graph.py boot Modal sandbox correctly.

signals.topic: CompositeBackend write/edit triggers self-induced DeprecationWarning on every call via dataclasses.replace
signals.summary: WriteResult and EditResult are dataclasses with files_update as a declared field. dataclasses.replace() passes the existing files_update=None back to __init__, which triggers a LangChainDeprecationWarning on every user write or edit call through CompositeBackend.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed self-induced bug that degrades user experience on every write/edit operation. The library's own code triggers a deprecation warning it owns, flooding user output on every file write through CompositeBackend. While only 1 issue, the warning fires per-call (not one-time), making it a pervasive noise issue. The suggested fix is simple (direct mutation instead of replace).

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend.write/edit emits self-induced files_update DeprecationWarning via dataclasses.replace
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug. On every CompositeBackend.write() or edit() call, DeprecationWarning fires: 'files_update was deprecated in deepagents 0.5.0'. Root cause: dataclasses.replace() forwards all declared fields including files_update=None to __init__, defeating the Unset sentinel. Downstream users see warning on every write/edit.

signals.topic: SSRF bypass via LANGCHAIN_ENV environment variable bypass in validate_safe_url (langchain-core)
signals.summary: validate_safe_url contains an exploitable bypass: when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test, any hostname matching startswith('test') and 'server' in hostname silently bypasses all SSRF checks. Also, _effective_allowed_hosts uses startswith('local') which incorrectly expands the allowlist for any env var prefixed with 'local', exposing cloud-metadata and private-IP endpoints to attackers.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports both confirm an active SSRF bypass in langchain-core's validate_safe_url. Exploitation requires only setting LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test (a common dev/test config), after which attacker-controlled hostnames bypass all SSRF protections including private-IP and cloud-metadata (169.254.169.254) checks. This is a direct, reproducible, high-severity security flaw with clear user impact (SSRF enables data exfiltration from internal services). Count=2 confirms this is not an isolated report.

source_issues.title: Bug: SSRF bypass in validate_safe_url when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows validate_safe_url('http://test.attacker.server.com/exfil') returns unchecked when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test. Root cause: startswith('test') and 'server' in hostname bypass predicate. Second issue: _effective_allowed_hosts uses startswith('local') silently expanding allowlist for any 'local_*' env var.

source_issues.title: Bug: exploitable SSRF bypass in validate_safe_url via LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test
source_issues.evidence: Detailed root cause: validate_safe_url raw-return bypass block skips all SSRF validation (scheme, private-IP, cloud-metadata checks) for attacker-controlled hostnames matching the local_test predicate. Full exploit path documented with working fix + regression tests ready.

signals.topic: Path traversal via unsanitized URI in Chroma.add_images() public API (langchain-chroma)
signals.summary: Chroma.add_images(uris=[...]) passes caller-supplied URIs directly to Path(uri).open('rb') with no path validation. Any caller with access to the public API can read arbitrary files from the filesystem (e.g., /etc/passwd), returning contents base64-encoded through the embeddings pipeline.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed arbitrary file read vulnerability in the langchain-chroma public API. The reproducer demonstrates reading /etc/passwd via path traversal (../../../../etc/passwd) without any error. The uris parameter is a public API accepting arbitrary caller input, making this exploitable by any user of the library. This is a critical security flaw with direct user impact (arbitrary filesystem read).

source_issues.title: Bug: path traversal in Chroma.add_images() via unsanitized URI
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer confirms store.add_images(uris=['../../../../etc/passwd']) reads arbitrary file and returns content base64-encoded with no error. Root cause: encode_image() calls Path(uri).open('rb') with no path validation. uris is part of the public API accepting any caller-supplied string. Working fix + unit tests available.

signals.topic: ChatOpenAI with Gemini models: multi-turn tool-calling broken due to missing thought_signature (400 BadRequestError)
signals.summary: When using ChatOpenAI with Gemini models (via base_url pointing to Google API), multi-turn tool-calling fails with 400 BadRequestError. Root cause: LangChain does not preserve the thought_signature field returned by Gemini in first-turn responses, causing subsequent turns to fail the API's required thought_signature validation for function calls.
aliases: Google Gemini thought signature not preserved across turns
signals.review_reason: Full-stack main flow failure: multi-turn tool-calling with Gemini models via ChatOpenAI is completely broken. Every multi-turn conversation using tools with Gemini 3 models will fail with a 400 error on the second turn. This blocks the primary use case of agentic tool-calling with Gemini through LangChain. Complete reproducer with stack trace confirms this is a library bug, not a user error.

source_issues.title: ChatOpenAI fails to provide thought signatures on multi-turn conversations when used with Gemini models, resulting in 400 BadRequestError
source_issues.evidence: Full reproducer with complete stack trace. Turn 1 succeeds; Turn 2 (continuing the conversation with ToolMessage) raises openai.BadRequestError 400 with message: 'Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts. This is required for tools to work correctly.' Google's documentation confirms: 'if you receive a thought signature in a model response, you should pass it back exactly as received when sending the conversation history in the next turn.' LangChain drops this field, breaking the core multi-turn tool-calling flow.

signals.topic: Mistral AI structured output broken: strict parameter causes 422 Unprocessable Entity error
signals.summary: Using ProviderStrategy with Pydantic schema for structured output on Mistral AI models throws 422 error. LangChain passes 'strict: true' to Mistral's API which does not accept this parameter (OpenAI-specific), causing every structured output call to Mistral to fail.
aliases: ProviderStrategy strict parameter not supported by Mistral
signals.review_reason: Structured output is a key functionality for Mistral AI integration. The bug causes 100% of structured output calls to Mistral to fail with a 422 error, making the feature completely unusable. The error is clearly a library bug (incorrect parameter propagation) rather than a user mistake. Complete reproducer with API error response confirms the issue.

source_issues.title: ProviderStrategy does not allow passing strict into the mistral ai JSON Schema response_format
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows 422 Unprocessable Entity from Mistral API: 'Extra inputs are not permitted, loc: [body, strict], input: true'. The strict parameter is an OpenAI-specific structured output feature that Mistral's API explicitly rejects. LangChain incorrectly propagates this parameter to Mistral, breaking structured output entirely for this provider.

signals.topic: SQL agent tutorial: stream_mode='values' interrupt handling branch never reached due to dict key ordering
signals.summary: The LangGraph SQL agent tutorial code checks 'if messages in step' before 'elif __interrupt__ in step', but with stream_mode='values' the step dict contains both keys simultaneously. The interrupt branch is therefore unreachable, causing the tutorial to never print interrupt output as documented.
aliases: SQL agent tutorial interrupt branch unreachable
LangGraph SQL agent docs example broken
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug in the official LangChain SQL agent tutorial documentation. The tutorial code will never reach the interrupt handling branch as written, breaking the expected user experience for anyone following the tutorial. While the workaround is documented in the issue, users who run the tutorial as-is will not see interrupt output as expected, causing confusion. P2 because count=1 and it's a docs issue in a single tutorial.

source_issues.title: A bug in learn-langgraph-SQL-agent
source_issues.evidence: User provides complete reproducer showing that when the graph reaches an interrupt, the streamed step contains both 'messages' and '__interrupt__'. The tutorial's if/elif chain always takes the 'messages' branch first, making the interrupt handling branch unreachable. Proposed fix: check __interrupt__ first before messages. This is a confirmed tutorial code bug in the official LangChain documentation.

signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization crashes — AIMessage TypeError (MemorySaver) and psycopg OperationalError (PostgresSaver)
signals.summary: Checkpointing crashes with TypeError when serializing AIMessage objects via MemorySaver msgpack path, and with psycopg OperationalError (SSL errors) when using PostgresSaver — both block the main agent execution flow.
aliases: Checkpoint serde TypeError with complex message types
Postgres checkpointer SSL connection failures during checkpoint writes
signals.review_reason: Both issues cause the main agent execution flow to crash at the checkpoint write step. #4956 blocks the core use case of MemorySaver with sub-agents returning AIMessage. #3716 blocks production workloads using PostgresSaver with SSL, affecting multiple versions. Both have reproducible stack traces and confirmed user impact.

source_issues.title: TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable: AIMessage
source_issues.evidence: When using MemorySaver with a sub-agent that returns AIMessage objects, the checkpoint serde path (msgpack encoder) raises TypeError, crashing the node that invokes the sub-agent. Stack trace shows the crash in MemorySaver.put_writes at serde/jsonplus.py. Main flow blocked.

source_issues.title: langgraph-checkpoint-postgres (psycopg.OperationalError: sending query and params failed: SSL error: bad length) encountered across multiple versions
source_issues.evidence: Postgres checkpointer raises psycopg.OperationalError with SSL errors during checkpoint writes. Users confirmed the issue across multiple versions (2.0.11, 2.0.9, 2.0.13, 2.0.15) and different langgraph versions. Task fails in production.

signals.topic: langgraph dev server cannot restart for ~60s after Ctrl+C due to TIME-WAIT socket reuse failure
signals.summary: After stopping `langgraph dev` with Ctrl+C, attempting to restart it immediately fails for ~60 seconds with 'Port 2024 already in use' even though no process is LISTENing — caused by TCP TIME-WAIT socket state not being reused.
aliases: langgraph dev port binding fails after quick restart
SO_REUSEADDR not used in langgraph_api port resolution
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow blocker for every developer using `langgraph dev`. After every Ctrl+C, the dev server becomes unstartable for ~60 seconds, forcing developers to either wait or kill the terminal. The root cause (missing SO_REUSEADDR in _resolve_port) is confirmed and a fix is identified.

source_issues.title: langgraph dev falsely reports 'Port 2024 already in use' due to TIME-WAIT entries
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: run langgraph dev, connect to studio, send message, hit Ctrl+C, try to restart immediately. OSError raised with message 'Port 2024 is already in use'. No process is actually LISTENing on the port — TCP TIME-WAIT state from the previous connection prevents rebinding. Workaround is waiting ~60s or rebooting. Stack trace shows failure in langgraph_api/cli.py:_resolve_port().

signals.topic: langgraph dev ignores graph checkpointer configuration, uses in-memory runtime, loses state on restart
signals.summary: The `langgraph dev` command ignores the checkpointer configured via `builder.compile(checkpointer=...)`, forcibly using `langgraph_runtime_inmem` instead, resulting in complete state loss after every restart or hot reload.
aliases: state persistence broken in langgraph dev
signals.review_reason: This causes data loss on every server restart during development. Users building stateful agents (the core use case for checkpointers) lose their entire conversation history each time they restart `langgraph dev` or trigger a hot reload. The startup logs explicitly confirm `langgraph_runtime_inmem` is used in place of the configured checkpointer.

source_issues.title: langgraph dev Ignores Checkpointer Configuration, Forcing In-Memory Storage and Preventing State Persistence
source_issues.evidence: User configures AsyncSqliteSaver via builder.compile(checkpointer=...), but startup logs show 'Using langgraph_runtime_inmem' and 'Starting In-Memory runtime'. The checkpoint.db file is created but remains empty. All state is lost on restart. This impacts development of any stateful conversational agent using langgraph dev.

signals.topic: graph.get_graph() crashes with TypeError sorting edges when combining Command[Literal[...]] returns with add_conditional_edges
signals.summary: Calling `graph.get_graph()` raises TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'str' when a node returns `Command[Literal[...]]` and the same node also uses `add_conditional_edges` — the sorted() calls in _draw.py cannot compare None vs str in the edge label field.
aliases: draw_graph TypeError with conditional edges and Command returns
signals.review_reason: This is a crash (TypeError) that makes the graph visualization feature entirely unusable for users combining Command[Literal[...]] returns with conditional edges — a common agent pattern. The bug is localized to two sorted() calls in _draw.py with a known fix.

source_issues.title: draw_graph: TypeError sorting edges with None data from conditional edges
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with minimal code: a node that returns Command(goto='node_a') combined with add_conditional_edges from the same node triggers TypeError in libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_draw.py when sorted() is called on NamedTuple edge lists with mixed None/str data fields. Versions 1.1.10 through 1.2.0a5 are affected.

signals.topic: Tool calls exceeding ~180s are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud, causing 2-3x redundant work and cost
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls lasting over ~180 seconds are silently re-executed from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both complete successfully, resulting in duplicate LLM calls, duplicate tool execution, and 2-3x inflated compute costs. Workaround attempts (BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS, asyncio.to_thread) are ineffective.
aliases: Silent re-execution of long-running tool calls from checkpoint
Background job sweep triggers duplicate task dispatch after 180s
signals.review_reason: This causes direct financial harm through silent 2-3x cost inflation on LangGraph Cloud. Long-running sub-agents (3-10 minutes) are a legitimate production use case, and the re-dispatch is completely invisible to users — they only notice when reviewing traces. The issue is persistent across multiple versions and multiple workarounds have been tried without success.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Users observe duplicate runs in LangSmith traces with identical tool call arguments (same content hash) but no preceding model node. The duplicate has its own tools node but is not triggered by an LLM decision — it is re-dispatched from checkpoint. Both original and duplicate complete successfully, wasting compute. Confirmed across langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6, EU Cloud, Plus tier. Workarounds BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS=900 and BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS=true had no effect. Root cause traced to BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 and the Runs.Sweep() mechanism in langgraph-api.

signals.topic: Dropdown menus in metadata filters and knowledge base search are obscured by other UI elements
signals.summary: Z-index layering bug causes dropdown menus to be hidden behind other UI elements, making filtering conditions unclickable.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation affecting knowledge base filtering - dropdown menus are unclickable due to z-index issues. Users cannot select metadata filtering conditions, blocking knowledge base search configuration. Reported in two separate contexts (metadata filter and KB search node) indicating a systematic UI layering bug introduced in a recent version.

source_issues.title: [Bug/UI] Dropdown menu in Metadata Filter is obscured by the 'Add Condition' button
source_issues.evidence: The dropdown list is overlapped by the '+ Add Condition' button. The dropdown menu should appear above all other elements (higher z-index) or the container should adjust its layout to ensure the dropdown list is fully visible.

source_issues.title: When using metadata in the knowledge base search node, it is not possible to select filtering conditions
source_issues.evidence: When clicking to select metadata type, the pop-up window is placed at a lower level, making it impossible to select. The previous version didn't have this issue.

signals.topic: Docker deployment high concurrency causes high latency, CPU overload, and request failures
signals.summary: Self-hosted Docker users experience extreme latency (up to 120s) and CPU overload failures under moderate concurrency (10-20 requests).
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - self-hosted Docker users experience up to 120s latency and request failures under moderate concurrency (10-20 simultaneous requests), with CPU overload at 99.3%. Repeated failures and latency indicate significant operational impact for users running agent workflows.

source_issues.title: The local Docker deployment method. After modifying the .env file, the concurrency cannot be improved. There is a high latency issue and even failures occur.
source_issues.evidence: When sending 10 concurrent requests instantly, the agent workflow delay is significantly sluggish, and it takes up to 60 seconds to complete the response. When 20 concurrent transmissions occur simultaneously, the delay can be as high as 120 seconds, and it may even directly show failure or CPU overload. Failed message shows system CPU overloaded (current: 99.3%, threshold: 90%).

signals.topic: Python code sandbox fails on default Docker deployment due to wrong Python path
signals.summary: Code execution sandbox misses /usr/local/bin/python3, breaking Python code interpreter on default Docker install.
signals.review_reason: Key feature unavailability - Python code execution (Code Interpreter, Python skills) fails out-of-the-box on default Docker deployment. Users must manually create symlinks as a workaround, indicating a broken default configuration that blocks code-based workflows.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Python code sandbox fails: '/usr/local/bin/python3: no such file or directory' - workaround available
source_issues.evidence: fork/exec /usr/local/bin/python3: no such file or directory. The code execution sandbox container may miss /usr/local/bin/python3, generating errors when code interpretation is triggered. Workaround requires manually creating symlinks inside the container.

signals.topic: History API returns incomplete conversation data - records are lost
signals.summary: API returns incomplete conversation history with missing records, while the same records are visible in the Dify UI.
signals.review_reason: Data integrity issue - API returns incomplete conversation history with missing records. Users cannot reliably retrieve conversation data through the API despite records existing in the UI. This is a data loss/cost loss issue for users relying on the API for audit or integration purposes.

source_issues.title: the history api lost data
source_issues.evidence: I've generated a lot of history after calling the application via API, but when I query those records through the API, many of them are often missing. The image shows conversation history visible in Dify UI differs from session list retrieved via API - records are lost.

signals.topic: TTS audio is truncated in SSE stream - only partial audio generated
signals.summary: TTS generates only the first sentence/paragraph of long model responses, breaking the auto-play audio feature.
signals.review_reason: Key feature degradation - TTS (text-to-speech) generates only partial audio, cutting off long model responses. This breaks the auto-play audio feature for chatflows and represents significant UX degradation for voice-enabled applications.

source_issues.title: [v1.13.3] TTS audio not generated in SSE stream; workflow_finished emitted before tts_message
source_issues.evidence: Only a partial TTS audio is generated (e.g., first sentence or paragraph), even though the LLM produced a much longer response. The /chat-messages API does not return TTS audio for the complete model output.

signals.topic: @mem0/openclaw-mem0 plugin ships unbuilt TypeScript — bricks OpenClaw gateway on install
signals.summary: The npm-published @mem0/openclaw-mem0 package contains only raw index.ts with no compiled dist/, no main/module fields, and no build scripts. Recent OpenClaw versions (2026.4.30+) hard-require compiled runtime output, causing the gateway to fail to start immediately after plugin installation with no working auto-fix.
aliases: gateway fails to start after plugin install
TypeScript not compiled in npm package
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues both reporting complete failure of the openclaw-mem0 plugin: #5106 blocks gateway startup entirely (non-bootable state) and #5069 makes memory features (autoRecall/autoCapture) unusable on Windows. Both are reproducible, affect the official npm package, and have no working remediation from the project side.

source_issues.title: @mem0/openclaw-mem0: published package ships unbuilt TypeScript; bricks OpenClaw gateway after recent plugin-validation tightening
source_issues.evidence: Gateway fails to start with 'plugin not found' error immediately after installing openclaw-mem0; openclaw doctor --fix does not auto-repair; workaround requires manual tsdown bundling and must be re-run on every reinstall.

source_issues.title: [Bug] @mem0/openclaw-mem0 v1.0.11 fails on Windows with OpenClaw 5.4: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME
source_issues.evidence: Plugin crashes with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME on Windows, making autoRecall and autoCapture entirely non-functional; workaround is to downgrade OpenClaw.

signals.topic: DockerHub OSS image outdated since Sept 2025 — users forced to use buggy version or build manually
signals.summary: The published DockerHub image (mem0/mem0-api-server) has not been updated since September 2025. Known bugs fixed in source code (e.g. update memory API dict/string mismatch) are absent from the image, forcing users to either use the SDK (Node/Python only), clone and self-host, or continuously monitor for changes.
aliases: OSS server image out of sync
signals.review_reason: Docker image has been stale for ~8 months with confirmed known bugs present in source but absent from published image. Users cannot pull a working version — this is a packaging release failure that directly blocks automated deployment workflows for any user relying on DockerHub images.

source_issues.title: Why has the Dockerhub Image for the OSS Rest API not been updated
source_issues.evidence: DockerHub image last updated September 2025; known bugs fixed in source not present in image; users must manually clone or use SDK, no automated update path.

signals.topic: Enterprise users blocked from local testing due to no native local/offline mode — forces external API calls incompatible with security/legal audits
signals.summary: mem0 has no first-party local mode. Enterprise users requiring data sovereignty cannot test the product without undergoing lengthy security and legal audits, as any agent interaction calls the mem0 API and potentially leaks source code or internal knowledge.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, the evidence shows a complete blocker for enterprise adoption: users cannot evaluate mem0 in a privacy-compliant environment. This is a primary use-case failure (enterprise self-hosting/local testing) with a clear workaround gap. Not P0 only because it's a single organizational testimony, not a mass-failure.

source_issues.title: Local mode
source_issues.evidence: Enterprise developer blocked from testing mem0 at their company due to no local/offline mode; agent calls mem0 API, leaking source code and internal tech knowledge without security/legal audit; workaround of using faiss+ollama locally exists but agent plugins don't work with it.

signals.topic: v3 ADD-only extraction pipeline produces stale/contradictory facts — agents receive outdated information
signals.summary: After upgrading to v3, the extraction pipeline is ADD-only: add() no longer emits UPDATE or DELETE events. For mutable facts (e.g. current employer, city), contradictory memories accumulate over time. Retrieval based on semantic similarity can rank the stale fact higher than the current one, leading to incorrect agent behavior.
signals.review_reason: Core memory correctness failure in v3: contradictory facts for the same entity coexist and the retrieval pipeline can surface the stale one. This directly causes incorrect agent responses in production (wrong employer, wrong city, etc.), which is a critical accuracy problem even at count=1. The bug is well-characterized with a concrete scenario.

source_issues.title: ADD-only extraction in v3 may surface stale/contradictory facts for time-sensitive attributes
source_issues.evidence: v3 extraction no longer emits UPDATE/DELETE events; user example: 'I work at Company A' stored 3 months ago coexists with 'I work at Company B' stored today; semantic search returns wrong company as top result because recency is not factored into scoring.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock boto3 client has no configurable timeout — large memory operations fail with read timeout
signals.summary: The AWSBedrockLLM class creates a boto3 client without timeout configuration, using botocore's default ~60s read timeout. Processing large memories (long conversations, complex extraction) consistently times out on Bedrock, especially with Claude Sonnet 4.
signals.review_reason: AWS Bedrock users experience confirmed read timeout failures when processing large memories — a well-documented error with a clear root cause. This is a production reliability issue for AWS Bedrock users, not an edge case, since large memory extraction is mem0's core use case. Confidence high given explicit error logs and detailed root-cause analysis.

source_issues.title: Add boto3 timeout configuration support for AWS Bedrock client
source_issues.evidence: Explicit error log: 'Failed to generate response: Read timeout on endpoint URL: bedrock-runtime.us-west-2.amazonaws.com' when processing large memories; AWS recommends 3600s read timeout for large model queries; no workaround available without modifying SDK internals.

signals.topic: Python: blocking synchronous tool execution freezes agent event loop and halts Responses API polling
signals.summary: When sync tools contain blocking code (e.g., time.sleep, long I/O), they execute directly inside the async event loop, freezing the entire loop. This causes Responses API polling to stop and the agent to appear frozen.
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks the main agent execution loop. The agent completely freezes and polling stops — this is a primary flow blocker confirmed with a concrete reproduction case.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Blocking synchronous tool execution freezes Responses API polling inside async event loop
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed reproduction: time.sleep(120) in a sync tool blocks the entire async event loop. Azure Bot polling the Responses API (GET endpoint) stops because polling runs in the same event loop. Agent appears frozen. Verified workaround: wrapping with asyncio.to_thread() fixes it.

signals.topic: .NET: telemetry/observability does not flow by default in Foundry hosted agent samples, requiring manual per-client enablement
signals.summary: In current Foundry/hosted agent .NET samples, telemetry traces do not flow by default. Customers must manually enable instrumentation at the client level. No traces are generated even when Azure Monitor exporter is configured.
signals.review_reason: Primary observability path is completely broken out of the box in Foundry hosting. This is a main-flow blocker for any production deployment relying on telemetry.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: MAF telemetry not flowing by default / requires per-client manual enablement
source_issues.evidence: User reports: no traces are generated even when TracerProvider with Azure Monitor trace exporter and APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING is configured. Instrumentation should auto-enable when any exporter is configured.

signals.topic: .NET: DurableTask SuperstepState.AccumulatedEvents exceeds 16KB CustomStatus cap causing orchestrator-level hard failure in multi-executor workflows
signals.summary: AccumulatedEvents in SuperstepState grows unbounded across supersteps and exceeds Durable Functions 16KB CustomStatus limit, causing orchestrator to hard-fail. Affects workflows with 6+ executors or large typed outputs like document processing and structured-response workflows.
signals.review_reason: Hard-fail orchestrator crash in production multi-executor workflows. Not a primary-flow issue for simple agents, but is a main flow blocker for structured-output and document-processing workflows — a documented real-world production failure.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: DurableTask: SuperstepState.AccumulatedEvents overflows CustomStatus 16 KB cap on multi-executor workflows with typed outputs
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced in production: Microsoft.Agents.AI.DurableTask 1.5.0-preview.260507.1 with 6+ sequential executors and typed outputs 1-4KB each. Fails at superstep 7 with 'CustomStatus is too large: limit = 16 KB (UTF-16), actual = 17.32 KB'. A concrete repro repo is available at connells-tech/ai-agent-runtime-dusty. Workarounds (enableStatusSlimming, bypassing orchestrator, splitting workflows) are all insufficient or require significant refactoring.

signals.topic: Python: OpenAIChatCompletionClient crashes with AttributeError when message.content is None during streaming
signals.summary: When using OpenAIChatCompletionClient with certain models (e.g. gpt-4.1), the client raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'content', causing the entire agent run to fail with ChatClientException.
signals.review_reason: Direct agent runtime crash with full stack trace. The agent completely fails to complete prompts with affected models, making agent streaming unusable for those model configurations.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: OpenAIChatCompletionClient exception
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace provided: AttributeError raised in _parse_text_from_openai at 'if message.content:'. ChatClientException wraps the error: 'NoneType object has no attribute content'. Agent run fails completely.

signals.topic: .NET: AgentSkillScript attribute regression — skill script methods stopped executing after upgrading to v1.5 (worked in v1.3)
signals.summary: After upgrading to version 1.5, skill script methods decorated with AgentSkillScript no longer execute. The scripts are not invoked and cannot be debugged. Regression from v1.3 which worked correctly.
aliases: skill script not executing after upgrade
signals.review_reason: Clear functional regression: skill scripts worked in v1.3, completely broken in v1.5. Silently fails with no error message, blocking agent functionality that depends on skill scripts.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]:
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports: '升級到1.5之後，skill的腳本方法沒辦法執行，之前1.3是可以的，現在skill腳本debug進不去，也不會執行'. AgentSkillScript decorated method (ConvertUnits) is silently not executed after v1.5 upgrade.

signals.topic: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
signals.summary: GroupChat speaker selection logic contains an off-by-one error causing the last agent to be skipped whenever max_round is an even number. With 3 agents and max_round=4, agent C never speaks — a deterministic, reproducible failure in the core group conversation routing.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed issues (7678, 7677, 7670) all reporting the same deterministic GroupChat speaker selection bug. An off-by-one error in the round-robin loop causes an agent to be systematically skipped when max_round is even — this is a core workflow failure that breaks multi-agent conversations in a predictable, reproducible way. Tested on autogen-agentchat 0.4.x. No workaround available.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Bug with reproducible steps: 3 agents, max_round=4, agent C never selected. Clear off-by-one error in speaker selection loop.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Exact duplicate of 7678 by same author.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Closed duplicate of 7678, same reproducible bug report.

signals.topic: Groq OpenAI-compatible API rejects structured output requests
signals.summary: AutoGen's OpenAIChatCompletionClient sends a response_format that Groq's API does not accept, resulting in a BadRequestError (400) when users attempt structured output with Groq models. The API returns: "'response_format.type' : value is not one of the allowed values ['text','json_object']".
signals.review_reason: Full stacktrace provided with complete reproduction code. The issue blocks structured output workflows with Groq models — a mainstream use case. Root cause is clear: AutoGen's model client sends a response_format.type that Groq doesn't support (only 'text' or 'json_object'). No workaround reported.

source_issues.title: Facing Issue while working with Groq openAI compatible endpoint
source_issues.evidence: Full traceback provided. AutoGen sends a response_format type (likely 'json_schema') that Groq's OpenAI compat endpoint does not support — only accepts 'text' or 'json_object'. Blocks structured output workflow.

signals.topic: Gemini/Vertex AI metadata size limit causes ResourceExhausted errors
signals.summary: When using Gemini 1.5-flash-002 via Vertex AI, AutoGen triggers a gRPC error: 'Metadata size exceeded hard limit (637301 vs. 16384 bytes)'. Users cannot use Gemini models through Vertex AI integration.
aliases: Gemini Vertex AI metadata hard limit error
signals.review_reason: A gRPC metadata size limit error (637KB vs 16KB hard limit) makes Gemini models entirely unusable via Vertex AI — a critical integration failure. User followed official documentation exactly and still hit the error. This is a hard block on a specific model provider path.

source_issues.title: Autogen when tried for Gemini model
source_issues.evidence: gRPC ResourceExhausted error: Metadata size 637301 bytes exceeds Vertex AI hard limit of 16384. User followed documentation exactly and still encountered the error. Gemini model completely unusable through Vertex AI in AutoGen.

signals.topic: WebKit on Windows hangs indefinitely when CONNECT proxy sends 407 and closes socket — no credential retry
signals.summary: When a HTTP CONNECT proxy responds with 407 Proxy Authentication Required and closes the TCP socket (standard proxy behavior), WebKit on Windows hangs until timeout instead of reconnecting with credentials. Chromium and Firefox handle this correctly. WebKit on Linux also handles it correctly. Only WebKit on Windows fails. Affects any test running through authenticated proxies on Windows.
aliases: WebKit CONNECT proxy authentication fails Windows
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm WebKit on Windows hangs with authenticated CONNECT proxies. This is a main-flow blocker for any test suite running through corporate proxies on Windows using WebKit. Chromium and Firefox work correctly. High impact for enterprise users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebKit on Windows hangs when CONNECT proxy closes socket after 407 doesn't reconnect with credentials
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo provided. Proxy logs show WebKit reconnects but sends CONNECT without Authorization header, gets 407 again, and hangs. Chromium succeeds. WebKit on Linux succeeds. Confirmed as a Windows-only WebKit issue with authenticated CONNECT proxies.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebKit on Windows hangs when CONNECT proxy closes socket after 407 doesn't reconnect with credentials
source_issues.evidence: Independent report of the same issue with a self-contained Node.js reproduction script. Same behavior: WebKit hangs on Windows when authenticated proxy closes socket after 407. Confirms it is a distinct reporter from 40768.

signals.topic: Client certificates regression — TLS handshake fails for non-certificate origins after v1.59.0 upgrade
signals.summary: Since v1.59.0, setting client_certificates for any origin causes Chromium to fail TLS handshake on ALL requests, including URLs that don't match the certificate origin. Previously only 1.58.0 worked. Root cause: the internal SOCKS proxy uses a self-signed certificate that now blocks all connections regardless of --ignore-certificate-errors.
aliases: Chromium TLS handshake failure with client certificates
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression (v1.58→v1.59) that completely breaks HTTPS testing workflows using client certificates. The internal SOCKS proxy now blocks all HTTPS connections, not just certificate-authenticated ones. This is a main-flow failure for any user with mTLS/client-certificate-based authentication in their test environment.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: client_certificates causing chromium to TLS handshake failure
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression from v1.58.0 to v1.59.0. Page.goto fails with ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED on all HTTPS URLs when client_certificates context option is set, even for origins not covered by the certificate. The internal SOCKS proxy's self-signed certificate blocks all connections.

signals.topic: playwright install hangs indefinitely on Node v26 — browser installation blocked
signals.summary: The playwright install command hangs forever when run on Node.js v26, preventing users from downloading/installing browsers. This blocks the entire getting-started experience for users on the latest Node version.
signals.review_reason: Playwright install hanging on Node v26 is a primary-flow blocker: users cannot install browsers on the latest Node.js version. This prevents new users from getting started and blocks existing users upgrading Node.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `playwright install` hangs in node v26
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction steps provided: install node 26, run npx playwright install, remove the .local-browsers directory, run npx playwright install again — it hangs. Blocks any user trying to use Playwright on the latest Node.js LTS.

signals.topic: CLI file arguments with spaces fail to match tests on Windows — absolute paths broken
signals.summary: On Windows, when passing absolute file paths containing spaces to 'npx playwright test', the CLI fails to find any tests (No tests found). Root cause: createFileMatcher() converts file paths to file:// URLs which percent-encode spaces, but the regex built from the CLI argument retains literal spaces, so they never match.
aliases: CLI path with spaces no tests found
signals.review_reason: This bug breaks test discovery for any path containing spaces on Windows, which is extremely common in enterprise/CI environments with user directories or build folders with spaces. The root cause is a clear encoding mismatch between file URLs and regex patterns.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: CLI file arguments with spaces in path fail to match on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproduction provided. Path 'C:\test dir\example.spec.mjs' fails with 'No tests found' on Windows while the same test with no spaces works. Affects any CI system or tool passing absolute paths to playwright test on Windows, including user profile directories like 'C:\Users\First Last\...'.

signals.topic: routeFromHAR records duplicate entries for retried requests — replay serves failed response, tests fail
signals.summary: When using routeFromHAR in recording mode and a request is retried after a transient failure, both the failed (empty-body) response and the successful retry are saved as separate entries for the same URL. On replay, Playwright serves the first (failed) entry, causing tests to receive blank pages.
signals.review_reason: HAR replay serving the wrong (failed) response causes test failures in the most common use case for routeFromHAR — offline/mock testing with flaky network conditions. This breaks test determinism and is a significant regression in the mock/offline testing workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: routeFromHAR records duplicate entries for retried requests, causing replay to serve failed response
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction repo provided. Simulates a server that destroys socket on first connection (transient failure) and returns 200 on retry. HAR file contains two entries for the same URL; replay serves the first (empty-body) one, so page.locator('h1') never matches 'Success', causing test failure.

signals.topic: KernelJsonSchema generation produces invalid schema (duplicate "null" type) for nullable enum parameters, causing HTTP 400 in strict-mode tool calls
signals.summary: Nullable enum parameters with null defaults produce a malformed JSON schema containing `["string", "null", "null"]` which fails validation by OpenAI strict mode, returning HTTP 400 invalid_function_parameters. This is a blocking failure for any user employing strict-mode model tool calls with nullable enum parameters.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: the schema generator emits an invalid JSON type array (`["string","null","null"]`) causing OpenAI strict mode to reject all tool calls using nullable enum parameters with null defaults. Users cannot use strict mode with these parameter patterns, blocking a critical AI model enforcement feature. Workaround (removing null default) is non-trivial in existing codebases.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Possible problem with KernelJsonSchema generation
source_issues.evidence: Schema produced: `"optionalEnumParam":{"type":["string","null","null"],"enum":["val1","val2","val3",null]}`. OpenAI strict mode returns HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error: invalid_function_parameters). Workaround: removing the null default. The bug is in KernelPluginFactory.CreateFromObject() schema generation for nullable enums with null defaults.

signals.topic: Documentation references non-existent CreateWithGetTextSearchResults overload in v1.7 preview, breaking documented usage
