Users following the docs hit a build failure with no resolution path.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point: official Microsoft documentation references an API overload that does not exist in the published v1.7 preview. Users following the docs experience build failures with no clear resolution, undermining trust in the documentation. The issue remains open and unresolved, directly blocking user productivity.

signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: .NETFramework users of the InMemory and SqliteVec connectors experience a build-time warning and a runtime FileLoadException when they attempt to use async APIs. signals.topic: Hover near right edge of Codex Desktop window triggers unexpected sidebar opening, disrupting copy/select workflows
signals.summary: The Codex Desktop app opens the right sidebar automatically when the mouse hovers near the right edge of the window. This is extremely disruptive during normal use: it covers content, steals visual focus, and makes basic text selection near the right side of the conversation feel unreliable. Two separate users filed duplicate reports.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users independently reported the same UX disruption. While not a workflow block, it 'interferes with frequent copy/select workflows' and 'is one of the most frustrating interaction patterns.' Count=2 meets the threshold for a pattern. Not P1 because it does not block core functionality and has a workaround (being careful about mouse position).

signals.topic: Windows Desktop + WSL workspace: unified_exec fails with ENOENT on /bin/bash, blocking shell tool execution
signals.summary: When Codex Desktop is configured with WSL-backed workspace on Windows, the unified_exec feature attempts to CreateProcess a Linux absolute path (/bin/bash) directly from the Windows process runner, resulting in os error 2 (ENOENT). All shell/tool commands fail before execution starts, breaking the primary user workflow. Workaround requires disabling unified_exec in config.
signals.review_reason: Core shell/tool workflow is completely blocked on Windows WSL hybrid setups. Every tool call fails with os error 2 before execution, making the primary coding loop unusable. Workaround (disabling unified_exec) exists but users should not need to manually fix this. Count=1 but impact is critical — primary workflow failure with no automatic recovery.

source_issues.title: Windows Desktop + WSL workspace: unified_exec tries to CreateProcess /bin/bash and fails with ENOENT
source_issues.evidence: CreateProcess fails with ENOENT on /bin/bash on every tool call. Workspace=/mnt/c/... on WSL2 Ubuntu. Shell tool completely blocked. Workaround: disable unified_exec. Related prior issues: #16970, #17240.

signals.topic: macOS reports Codex as malware, preventing app from opening
signals.summary: macOS security system (Gatekeeper/Notarization) reports Codex Desktop as malware when users attempt to open it after an update, showing a modal error. The app cannot be used at all until the user manually bypasses the macOS malware warning.
signals.review_reason: App is completely unusable for affected macOS users — the app literally cannot be opened. This is a complete workflow block. While it is a macOS platform false positive, the user experience impact is equivalent to a crash/block. Count=1 but severity is critical: primary entry point to Codex is broken.

source_issues.title: Malware "Cannot open Codex because of a malware" detected by macos
source_issues.evidence: User cannot open Codex at all. macOS malware modal appears during app launch after update. Affects users on latest version 26.506.31421. Requires manual bypass to use the app.

signals.topic: Sandbox approval '(p) don't ask again' persists permanently across sessions and workspaces, creating unexpected security exposure
signals.summary: When users approve a sandbox command using the '(p)' option ('don't ask again for commands that start with X'), the approval persists permanently across all future Codex sessions and across different workspaces. The prompt wording implies an in-session scope but the actual behavior is machine-wide and never expires. Users who habitually pick (p) to silence prompts create durable allow-rules without realizing the scope.
signals.review_reason: Security boundary violation: users cannot reasonably infer from the prompt that a single approval grants permanent cross-workspace access. Creates unexpected permanent allow-rules. This is a meaningful authorization scope defect, not a minor UX issue. Count=1 but the security risk and the discrepancy between prompt wording and actual behavior warrants P1.

source_issues.title: Approval prompt (p) "don't ask again" persists across sessions and workspaces with program-name-only scope
source_issues.evidence: Single (p) approval grants permanent cross-session and cross-workspace allow on the program name. Approval is persisted in config.toml and never re-prompted. Prompt wording 'commands that start with X' implies narrow scope; actual scope is machine-wide permanently.

signals.topic: Codex self-correction loops charge users for retry/recovery work caused by agent's own tool failures
signals.summary: When Codex's tool execution fails (e.g., file edit fails) and the agent explicitly detects this failure and retries using a different strategy, the retry and recovery work still counts against the user's usage quota and rate limits. Users absorb the cost of the platform's own instability. This happens consistently during normal daily use.
signals.review_reason: Users are charged for agent-initiated recovery work that results from platform/tool failures, not from user requests. This is an ambiguous billing model that causes consistent cost loss during normal use. The agent explicitly acknowledges failure and retries autonomously — users have no control over this. Count=1 but the financial impact and frequency (daily use) make this P1.

source_issues.title: Users should not absorb usage from Codex self-correction loops
source_issues.evidence: Agent explicitly detects failure ('The file was not changed') and autonomously retries with different strategy. All retry/recovery work counts against user quota and rate limits. Happens consistently during normal daily use, creating persistent cost burden.

signals.topic: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output, causing model to wait indefinitely
signals.summary: When a known function tool invocation raises an exception (including ToolTimeoutError), the session does not send RealtimeModelSendToolOutput back to the model. The model waits indefinitely until server-side timeout fires (~30 seconds). During this time the session appears to hang.
aliases: known tool exception no model output
signals.review_reason: Critical user blocker: model hangs indefinitely waiting for a tool result that never arrives after a known tool failure. This is a hard failure that makes realtime sessions completely unusable when tools fail. High severity despite single occurrence because the impact is session-level hang with no recovery.

source_issues.title: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output
source_issues.evidence: When a known function tool invocation raises an exception (including ToolTimeoutError), the session does not send RealtimeModelSendToolOutput back to the model. The model waits indefinitely until server-side timeout fires (~30 seconds). During this time the session appears to hang.

signals.topic: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped, replaced with generic HITL rejection message
signals.summary: Local tool on_approval callbacks can return a rejection reason, but that reason is dropped before the rejection output is generated. The run records the tool call as rejected, yet the model-visible tool output falls back to the generic HITL rejection message instead of the callback's reason.
signals.review_reason: User pain: when local tools are rejected via on_approval callbacks, the specific rejection reason provided by the callback is silently dropped and replaced with generic text. This degrades the model's ability to understand why an action was rejected, directly impacting the quality of subsequent agent decisions in human-in-the-loop workflows.

source_issues.title: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped
source_issues.evidence: Local tool on_approval callbacks can return a rejection reason, but that reason is dropped before the rejection output is generated. The run records the tool call as rejected, yet the model-visible tool output falls back to the generic HITL rejection message instead of the callback's reason.

signals.topic: AgentOutputSchema.name() crashes for Literal output types, breaking agent traces for valid structured output
signals.summary: AgentOutputSchema.name() crashes with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__name__' when the output type includes typing.Literal values. The schema can be built but name() fails during agent trace.
signals.review_reason: User pain: valid structured output types using typing.Literal cause a crash in AgentOutputSchema.name(), breaking agent traces for otherwise correct output schemas. This is a runtime crash in a core feature (tracing) triggered by a perfectly valid type annotation.

source_issues.title: AgentOutputSchema.name() fails for Literal output types
source_issues.evidence: AgentOutputSchema.name() crashes with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__name__' when the output type includes typing.Literal values. The schema can be built but name() fails during agent trace.

signals.topic: AdvancedSQLiteSession.add_items reports success but messages are invisible to get_items due to metadata failure
signals.summary: add_items() writes rows to base messages table, commits, then writes message_structure rows. If structure metadata write fails, add_items() logs error and returns without raising. Callers observe success but get_items() cannot read the saved messages because advanced reads join through message_structure.
signals.review_reason: Data integrity bug: session save appears successful to callers but messages are silently lost from future reads. This creates an undetectable failure mode where retry logic cannot reliably know whether to retry or stop, potentially causing duplicate submissions or lost agent context.

source_issues.title: AdvancedSQLiteSession.add_items can report success after structure metadata failure
source_issues.evidence: add_items() writes rows to base messages table, commits, then writes message_structure rows. If structure metadata write fails, add_items() logs error and returns without raising. Callers observe success but get_items() cannot read the saved messages because advanced reads join through message_structure.

signals.topic: Missing per-run budget guard for token/request/cost limits - runaway agents can make thousands of API calls unchecked
signals.summary: Real production pain: an agent loop triggered thousands of unexpected API calls before anyone noticed. Users explicitly asked for hard budget guardrails as a pre-deployment gate. Using result.usage after the run is too late; org-level budget is too coarse and does not protect per-customer/tenant flows.
signals.review_reason: Real production blocker documented by users: runaway agents making thousands of API calls before detection causes significant unplanned cost. Users need per-run budget enforcement as a pre-deployment gate to prevent cost overrants in multi-tenant scenarios. This is a feature request with documented production incident evidence.

source_issues.title: Proposal: per-run BudgetGuard for token / request / cost limits (follow-up to #2848)
source_issues.evidence: Real production pain: an agent loop triggered thousands of unexpected API calls before anyone noticed. Users explicitly asked for hard budget guardrails as a pre-deployment gate. Using result.usage after the run is too late; org-level budget is too coarse and does not protect per-customer/tenant flows.

signals.topic: Streaming tool_call 累积逻辑无法正确处理首 chunk 中相同 index 的多条目，导致 function.arguments JSON 解析失败
signals.summary: 在 v2.35.0 中，当 streaming chunk 包含两个相同 index 的 tool_calls 条目时，accumulate_delta 将其存储为两个独立列表元素而非合并。后续 chunk 只合并到 index 0，留下孤立的 index 0 条目，导致 function.arguments 无法解析为合法 JSON。使用 vLLM+speculative decoding 时触发。
signals.review_reason: count=2，高频；主流程阻断（streaming tool call 是核心功能）；同 index 重复条目导致 function.arguments JSON 损坏，工具调用参数不可用；已提供可复现代码，影响 openai/openai-python 用户通过 vLLM 等兼容服务器使用 speculative decoding 的场景。

source_issues.title: `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when one chunk has multiple entries at the same `index`
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed with reproduction code: duplicate index 0 entries in first chunk cause orphaned entry, resulting in malformed JSON arguments not parseable by json.loads()

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk are accumulated incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed with reproduction steps using vLLM+speculative decoding: arguments end up split across two physical list entries with the same index, final JSON is invalid

signals.topic: v2.34.0 引入破坏性变更：api_key="" 不再被接受，导致所有本地兼容服务器的 SDK 客户端初始化失败
signals.summary: v2.34.0 新增凭证验证逻辑后，AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") 改为抛出 OpenAIError: Missing credentials。大量使用 OpenAI 兼容本地服务器（llama.cpp、llamafile、LM Studio、vLLM 等）的用户受影响，因为这些场景本不需要认证。
signals.review_reason: count=1，但有明确强用户影响证据：v2.34.0 破坏性变更，所有使用本地兼容服务器（无认证场景）的用户均受影响；主流程阻断（客户端无法初始化）；v2.33.0 及之前版本正常工作，回退到 v2.33.0 是目前唯一解；review_reason 明确给出强用户影响证据，可突破 count<3 的默认限制。

source_issues.title: AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError in v2.34.0, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers
source_issues.evidence: Breaking change in v2.34.0: passing api_key="" to AsyncOpenAI now raises OpenAIError instead of being silently accepted. Workaround is api_key="not-needed" but this is a regression from all prior versions. All local OpenAI-compatible server users are affected (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM).

signals.topic: Responses API 多轮对话中将 response.output.model_dump() 作为 input 回传时 turn 2 抛出 400 错误（fabricate null unknown fields）
signals.summary: 使用 model_dump() 将 response.output 回传为下一轮 input 时，model_dump() 额外生成了 API 未返回的 null 字段（如 status: None、encrypted_content: None），API 在 turn 2 时以 400 Unknown parameter 拒绝。此外存在 reasoning+message 配对约束，单独过滤消息也会触发 400。
aliases: response output as input null fields
signals.review_reason: 核心多轮对话功能阻断；model_dump() 生成非法字段导致 API 400；影响范围广（openai-agents-python、pydantic-ai、OpenClaw 均受影响）；open since Aug 2025 无修复；review_reason 明确说明用户影响。

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug: model_dump() on response.output generates fabricated null fields (status: None, encrypted_content: None) that cause 400 Unknown parameter on turn 2. Downstream SDKs affected: openai-agents-python, pydantic-ai, OpenClaw (64.9k forks). Spec root cause tracked in openai/openai-openapi#536. Workaround: use previous_response_id instead.

signals.topic: AsyncResponses.parse() 使用 Pydantic 模型时存在内存泄漏：TypeVar 未解析导致每次调用都重新分配重型 Rust SchemaValidator 对象
signals.summary: openai/lib/_parsing/_responses.py 中使用 TypeVar 参数化的 ParsedResponse[TextFormatT] 调用 construct_type_unchecked，Pydantic 无法解析未绑定的 TypeVar，model_rebuild 始终返回 False，MockCoreSchema._built_memo 从未被填充，每次调用都创建新的 SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer（重量级 Rust 对象），内存无限增长最终 OOM。
signals.review_reason: 长运行服务内存无限增长最终 OOM（关键功能不可用/成本损失）；已提供 flame graph 证据和根因分析；影响所有使用 AsyncResponses.parse() + Pydantic 的用户；review_reason 明确说明用户影响。

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed memory leak in AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic models. Root cause: TypeVar TextFormatT unresolved causes model_rebuild to always return False, preventing _built_memo cache population. Each call allocates new SchemaValidator/Rust objects that never get freed. Flame graph provided. Long-running servers will OOM.

signals.topic: ResponseFunctionWebSearch 类型定义与实际返回 payload 不匹配：action 字段可为 None 但类型声明禁止该值
signals.summary: SDK 类型定义中 ResponseFunctionWebSearch 的 action 字段声明为不可为 None，但实际 API 返回中部分 web_search_call 的 action 为 None（已观察到 4 个 web search 中后 2 个 action=None）。用户代码基于类型签名假设 action 存在，执行 item.action.type == "search" 时触发 AttributeError。
signals.review_reason: 类型与实际返回不匹配导致 AttributeError；影响依赖 action.type 判断搜索结果的代码；已提供可复现代码。

source_issues.title: ResponseFunctionWebSearch doesn't match returned payload
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed type/payload mismatch: ResponseFunctionWebSearch.action is typed as non-nullable but actual API returns action=None for some web_search_calls. User code raising error: sum(1 for item in raw_response.output if item.type == 'web_search_call' and item.action.type == 'search') raises AttributeError.

signals.topic: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED while direct acpx claude succeeds
signals.summary: The OpenClaw spawn path for Claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED/Internal error even though the same operation succeeds via direct acpx claude, blocking the automatic two-agent ACP flow.
aliases: ACP turn failure in OpenClaw path
signals.review_reason: Main flow is explicitly blocked: the OpenClaw spawn path for Claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED while the identical operation via direct acpx claude succeeds on the same host. This is not a degraded experience — it is a complete workflow failure that prevents the two-agent ACP flow. The issue provides concrete reproduction steps, environment details, and clearly identifies the blocking nature with a manual workaround. This is a P0 despite count=1 because the user explicitly states automatic two-agent flow is blocked, which is a primary use case.

source_issues.title: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED while direct acpx claude succeeds
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude --mode oneshot returns ACP_TURN_FAILED / UNAVAILABLE / Internal error. Direct acpx claude from same host succeeds. signals.topic: Sessions history API does not reflect live assistant/tool events during active turn, forcing orchestrators to parse rollout logs directly
signals.summary: While an agent is actively running, sessions history only shows user prompts but not streamed assistant/tool events, even though those events exist in the rollout JSONL on disk. This breaks the natural polling workflow for programmatic orchestration.
aliases: Session history incomplete during live turn
Assistant/tool events not checkpointed in session history
Sessions history API lacks live progress visibility
signals.review_reason: This is a functional gap rather than a complete block: the agent still runs and produces results, but the sessions history API does not provide a live view during the turn. The issue explicitly states orchestrators must 'fall back to parsing the rollout log directly' — this degrades the orchestration experience significantly for the key programmatic use case. However, the core agent functionality is not blocked, so it is P2 rather than P0/P1. The review_reason must distinguish this: the agent runs to completion and produces correct output, but the session history API contract is incomplete during live execution.

source_issues.title: ACP session history only records prompts while Codex is running
source_issues.evidence: sessions history shows only user prompt during an active turn; assistant messages, tool calls, and tool outputs are absent even though the rollout log on disk contains them. lsof and tail confirmed codex-acp is actively writing events. Orchestrators must fall back to parsing the rollout JSONL directly instead of using the sessions history API as the natural polling mechanism.

signals.topic: CLI 参数和确认机制在非交互环境（LLM agent）中静默绕过安全控制
signals.summary: 两个独立技能中的安全控制被发现在 LLM agent 环境中可被静默绕过：imessage 的 force=true 参数跳过所有授权检查直接发送消息；context-restore 的 --confirm 在非交互环境下自动 approve，致使用户确认机制形同虚设。
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 均描述了真实的安全控制绕过行为，具有明确用户影响证据：force=true 让 agent 能在未经用户授权情况下直接发送消息；--confirm 在 agent 环境中静默自动通过确认。这不是误报或功能请求，而是两个技能中确实存在的授权绕过漏洞，违反了用户预期的安全门控。均处于 open 状态，等待处理。

source_issues.title: Security: `force=true` bypasses all security checks (lilei0311/imessage)
source_issues.evidence: imessage skill 的 send_message() 接受 force=true 参数，当为 true 时跳过 authorize_send() 的所有检查（可信联系人验证、日限额、isatty 确认）。在 LLM agent 环境中，agent 遇到授权错误后会读取源码发现 force 参数并利用它绕过所有安全控制。ClawScan 报告 SAFE(0/100)，但实际存在结构性授权绕过漏洞。

source_issues.title: Security: Skill context-restore fallback bypass user confirmation
source_issues.evidence: context-restore skill 的 --confirm 标志在非交互环境（LLM agent、CI/CD、cron）中，input() 抛出 EOFError，except 块静默设置 confirmation='y'。该技能设计用于 agent 工作流，但确认机制在主要使用场景中完全失效，用户误以为有安全门控实际形同虚设。

signals.topic: 包发布流程被 runtimeId 不可变更性和 publisher 不存在问题阻断
signals.summary: 两个独立问题导致包无法发布：(1) ClawHub 将 runtimeId 视为首次发布后不可变的，导致占位符 runtimeId 错误时包永久绑定到错误 ID，无法纠正；(2) @clawkit publisher 不存在，导致 3 个已有包无法发布新版本。
aliases: publisher namespace does not exist blocks release
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 均提供了明确的阻断证据（CLI 错误输出），影响包发布主流程，属于关键功能不可用。#2133 的 runtimeId 不可变更问题持续阻断 openviking 插件发布；#2114 使 3 个 clawkit 包无法更新到新版本。但两个问题针对不同根因（runtimeId 不可变 vs publisher 不存在），count=2 为精确去重。优先级 P1 而非 P0 因影响范围相对有限（均为特定包/组织）。

source_issues.title: Allow safe runtimeId correction for placeholder code-plugin packages
source_issues.evidence: @openviking/openclaw-plugin 的 runtimeId 被设为占位符 openviking-openclaw-plugin-placeholder，真实插件的 runtimeId 应为 openviking。发布真实插件时失败：'Package already exists with plugin id openviking-openclaw-plugin-placeholder; runtime id changes are not allowed'。包名永久绑定到不可用的 runtimeId，后续发布被持续阻断，且软删除也无法解决。

source_issues.title: Create or claim @clawkit publisher for existing ClawKit packages
source_issues.evidence: 3 个已有 @clawkit/* 包（clawkit-for-lovable 0.1.11、clawkit-for-whisprai、clawkit-creative-studio）的发布被阻断：'This package name uses the "@clawkit" namespace, but that publisher does not exist on ClawHub'。--owner marcsean1971 不匹配 @clawkit scope，--owner clawkit 失败因为 publisher 不存在。dry-run 成功但实际发布失败。

signals.topic: 技能搜索前缀匹配架构性缺陷导致非首 token 关键词永远无法匹配，搜索结果随时间衰减不可预测
signals.summary: 搜索系统依赖 4 条字符串前缀查询，仅当搜索词是技能 slug/displayName 的首 token 前缀时才匹配。当用户搜索非首 token（如「yijian」「vision」）时返回零结果；此外，基于 updatedAt 的 recency 窗口使技能在发布新版本后短暂可见，随后因其他技能更新而被挤出窗口再次消失。
aliases: search prefix index only matches first token
visibility decay based on updatedAt window
signals.review_reason: Issue #2137 提供了详尽的代码级根因分析，涵盖 3 条独立召回路径的失效机制，并给出了具体修复方案。搜索是技能发现的主流程，结构性缺陷意味着任何不以搜索词为首 token 的技能都永久不可发现，且可见性随时间不可预测地波动。属于主流程阻断性缺陷（count=1 但影响覆盖所有技能）。

source_issues.title: [Search] Skill search underrecall: non-first-token keywords never match, visibility decays over time
source_issues.evidence: 代码审查确认 convex/search.ts 的 directPrefixSkillMatches 对 baidu-yijian-vision 查询「yijian」返回零结果，因为所有 4 条前缀查询的 firstToken 均为「baidu」。lexicalFallbackSkills 依赖 updatedAt recency 窗口，新版本发布后技能短暂可见，随后随其他技能更新被挤出窗口再次消失。这是一个结构性架构缺陷，非边缘案例，影响所有非首 token 搜索。

source_issues.title: Dashboard does not expose org publisher packages after transfer/publish

signals.topic: Quick Send dialog titlebar styling inconsistency and focus/z-order blocking user interaction
signals.summary: Quick Send dialog (Ctrl+Shift+O / tray menu) does not extend content into the titlebar unlike Hub/Canvas windows, causing mismatched styling and dark mode issues. Additionally, the dialog stays on top of z-order, does not light-dismiss, and interferes with the tray icon right-click menu flyout, forcing users to manually dismiss it with Escape or Cancel.
signals.review_reason: Real user-experienced bug: Quick Send dialog blocks core tray interaction (tray menu flyout cannot open while dialog is up) and fails to light-dismiss, forcing manual Escape/Cancel. Titlebar styling inconsistency with dark mode is a visible UX regression compared to Hub/Canvas windows. Count=1 (single issue) and single repo, so P1 (not P0) despite being a confirmed UX blocking issue.

source_issues.title: Quick Send dialog: titlebar styling mismatch, focus/z-order issues
source_issues.evidence: Quick Send dialog has titlebar styling mismatch (does not use custom 48px titlebar like Hub/Canvas), dark mode mismatch, focus-stealing behavior that prevents tray menu flyout from opening, and no light-dismiss on focus loss. Workaround requires manual Escape/Cancel. Reproduced on Windows 11 ARM64.

signals.topic: Matrix dependency bootstrap can delete global OpenClaw installation by running npm install from unsafe parent directories
signals.summary: Matrix extension's deps.ts computes install cwd using fixed '../..' traversal from the compiled file, potentially running `npm install` from an unintended parent directory. npm treats the parent as project root and removes existing global packages, deleting the globally installed openclaw package and leaving the CLI symlink dangling.
aliases: npm from global node_modules deletes packages
signals.review_reason: Destructive system-level failure — the Matrix dependency bootstrap can completely delete the global openclaw installation from disk. Two separate issues (#80754, #80758) independently describe the same unsafe '../..' traversal pattern. Explicitly marked as a beta blocker. count=2 after deduplication.

source_issues.title: Matrix dependency bootstrap can delete global OpenClaw install by running npm install from global node_modules
source_issues.evidence: cwd set to global npm node_modules directory (e.g., /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules). npm treats parent as project root, reifies empty project, removes existing global packages including openclaw. CLI symlink left dangling.

source_issues.title: Beta blocker: Matrix runtime dependency repair still runs npm from unsafe parent directories
source_issues.evidence: Matrix runtime dependency fallback computes install cwd via fixed '../..' traversal from compiled file, running npm install from unintended parent directory. Explicitly marked as beta blocker.

signals.topic: Telegram session: heartbeat fired in group chat causes permanent message delivery failure
signals.summary: A heartbeat event fired in a Telegram group session instead of the main session. OpenClaw recorded `pendingFinalDelivery: "HEARTBEAT_OK"` in sessions.json, causing the session to become permanently stuck — all subsequent responses were generated but never delivered to Telegram.
signals.review_reason: Permanent message delivery failure — a user-facing blocking issue where a Telegram session becomes permanently stuck after a heartbeat event misfires in a group context. All subsequent responses are generated server-side but silently dropped, leaving users with no indication of failure.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Heartbeat fires in Telegram group session, causes permanent delivery failure
source_issues.evidence: Heartbeat response recorded as pendingFinalDelivery in sessions.json → session permanently stuck → all responses generated but never delivered to Telegram. Session becomes permanently non-functional.

signals.topic: Plaintext API tokens (Slack xoxb-/xapp-, Telegram bot tokens) persist indefinitely in append-only config-audit.jsonl log
signals.summary: PR #75095 added redaction for newly written audit entries, but config-audit.jsonl is append-only with no rotation or scrub. Users who ran `openclaw config set` with secret values between Feb 14 and May 1 2026 have live credentials sitting in plaintext on disk indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: Credential exposure at rest — live API tokens (Slack xoxb tokens, Telegram bot tokens) persist in plaintext in an append-only audit log file on disk. Any file-system compromise or log sharing exposes these credentials. The exposure window spans months (Feb–May 2026) for affected users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: pre-`#75095` plaintext-token entries in `~/.openclaw/logs/config-audit.jsonl` are never scrubbed after upgrade
source_issues.evidence: Append-only audit log with no rotation or scrub. Plaintext Slack (xoxb-/xapp-), Telegram bot tokens, and other secrets from pre-upgrade commands persist on disk indefinitely. No automatic cleanup mechanism exists.

signals.topic: Image-understanding deadline collapses to 1ms causing indefinite tight retry loop
signals.summary: When image description times out, `Math.max(1, remainingBudget)` forces the next retry's timeout to 1ms, causing immediate re-rejection and a self-reinforcing tight loop that consumes resources continuously for 6+ hours per image.
signals.review_reason: Resource-wasting indefinite retry loop — once an image description times out, the deadline budget collapses to 1ms, causing a self-reinforcing tight retry loop that runs for 6+ hours per image. Wastes API quota and compute without producing any result.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: image-understanding deadline budget collapses to 1ms via Math.max(1, …), causing tight retry loop
source_issues.evidence: resolveImageDescriptionTimeoutMs computes negative remaining budget and clamps to 1ms via Math.max(1, ...). Next call has timeoutMs=1ms → immediate timeout → rejection → repeat. Observed causing 6+ hour continuous retry loops per image.

signals.topic: createFollowupRunner bypasses cliBackends config causing Anthropic third-party billing classification and multi-hour cooldowns
signals.summary: createFollowupRunner unconditionally calls runEmbeddedPiAgent, ignoring agents.defaults.cliBackends. Follow-up messages go through OpenClaw's embedded SDK client, which Anthropic classifies as third-party app and bills from the paid extra-usage pool instead of plan limits, causing HTTP 402 errors and multi-hour cooldowns.
signals.review_reason: Direct financial impact and service outage — users lose plan quota benefits and face HTTP 402 errors with multi-hour cooldowns affecting ALL API calls under the same auth profile. This is a high-frequency recurring issue for any multi-turn conversation.

source_issues.title: createFollowupRunner bypasses cliBackends config → embedded runner hits Anthropic third-party billing classification
source_issues.evidence: Follow-up messages routed through OpenClaw embedded SDK client, misclassified by Anthropic as third-party app. Results in HTTP 402 errors and multi-hour cooldowns that block ALL calls using that auth profile. No plan quota utilization.

signals.topic: Long command-line arguments (--system-prompt, --custom-instruction) cause OSError at startup on macOS
signals.summary: When users pass long system prompts or custom instructions via CLI arguments, pathlib.Path() misinterprets argv strings as file paths and raises OSError [Errno 63] File name too long at startup, completely blocking aider from launching.
aliases: OSError file name too long at startup
signals.review_reason: This is a startup-blocking crash where aider fails to launch entirely when users pass long system prompts or custom instructions via CLI. The root cause is that main.py passes argv elements (which include long flag values) directly to Path.is_dir(), and the OS treats these strings as file paths subject to path length limits. Three separate users on macOS reported this same OSError with different long argument values, confirming high frequency and real-world impact. This is a primary use-case failure — users relying on system prompts for persona/configuration cannot start aider at all.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 840
source_issues.evidence: OSError [Errno 63] File name too long triggered by '--custom-instruction' argument being passed to Path(all_files[0]).is_dir() on macOS

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 840
source_issues.evidence: OSError [Errno 63] File name too long triggered by '--system-prompt-prefix' argument being passed to Path(all_files[0]).is_dir() on macOS

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 840
source_issues.evidence: OSError [Errno 63] File name too long triggered by '--system-prompt' argument being passed to Path(all_files[0]).is_dir() on macOS

signals.topic: aiohttp ConnectionTimeoutError AttributeError crashes aider at startup on Windows
signals.summary: On certain Windows environments, importing litellm triggers an aiohttp import that raises AttributeError because aiohttp has no 'ConnectionTimeoutError' attribute, crashing aider immediately at startup.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete startup-blocking crash for affected Windows users. Aider cannot even begin execution because the AttributeError is raised during the dependency import chain (runpy -> models.Model -> litellm.validate_environment -> litellm._load_litellm -> import litellm -> aiohttp_transport). The error originates from a version mismatch between the installed aiohttp and what aiohttp_transport.py expects, causing aider to be completely unusable on affected Windows environments.

source_issues.title: Uncaught AttributeError in __init__.py line 240
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: module aiohttp has no attribute 'ConnectionTimeoutError' raised during litellm import in aiohttp_transport.py line 23, at models.py validate_environment(), blocking entire aider startup on Windows 10 with CPython 3.11.4

signals.topic: Windows console output crashes with UnicodeEncodeError during interactive sessions
signals.summary: On Windows, when the Rich console writes output containing surrogate characters, it raises uncaught UnicodeEncodeError with 'surrogates not allowed', cascading into an unhandled exception loop that crashes the entire interactive session.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking crash that occurs mid-interactive-session on Windows. The UnicodeEncodeError cascades through three exception layers (io._tool_message -> console._exit_buffer -> _write_buffer) without being caught, resulting in an unhandled crash. The user cannot complete their chat interaction and the session terminates entirely. PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 is suggested as a workaround but is not automatically applied.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in console.py line 2097
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 2828-2829: surrogates not allowed in console.py _write_buffer(), cascading into three uncaught exception layers during a chat command execution, crashing the entire interactive session on Windows 11 with CPython 3.12.13

signals.topic: tree-sitter QueryError crashes repo-map generation on Windows with certain language files
signals.summary: On Windows, repomap.py's tree-sitter tag extraction raises an uncaught QueryError 'Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module', preventing the repository map from being built and breaking the core repo analysis feature.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional-blocking crash for the repo-map feature on Windows. The QueryError originates from tree-sitter language bindings and propagates up through get_tags_raw -> get_tags -> get_ranked_tags -> get_ranked_tags_map_uncached -> get_ranked_tags_map -> get_repo_map, breaking the entire repo map generation pipeline. Since repo-map is a core feature that informs the LLM about the codebase, its failure disrupts the primary aider workflow.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module raised in repomap.py get_tags_raw() during repo-map generation on Windows 11 with Python 3.12.10, crashing the get_repo_map() pipeline which is called from format_chat_chunks() in the main message-sending flow

signals.topic: Windows console stdout flush OSError crashes send-message output streaming
signals.summary: On Windows, sys.stdout.flush() raises OSError [Errno 22] Invalid argument during output streaming in show_send_output_stream, causing an unhandled exception that crashes the interactive message-sending flow.
aliases: stdout flush OSError Windows streaming crash
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking crash during the active message exchange phase on Windows. The OSError occurs in the stdout flush call within the send-message output stream rendering loop, cascades through the Rich console write path, and crashes the entire interactive session without recovery. Users lose their in-progress conversation.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in _win32_console.py line 403
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument at sys.stdout.flush() in show_send_output_stream on Windows 11, cascading through base_coder.py send_message flow, uncaught during output rendering in _win32_console.write_text()

signals.topic: Realtime models do not trigger tool/function calls
signals.summary: When using the OpenAI realtime provider (e.g., openai:realtime:gpt-realtime), configured tools are not invoked — the model returns plain text instead of calling the defined tool. The same tool configuration works correctly with the chat provider (openai:chat:gpt-4o-mini), indicating a broken parity between realtime and chat model providers in Promptfoo.
signals.review_reason: This is a core feature gap where realtime models completely fail to trigger tool calls, a key Promptfoo capability. The user demonstrates that the same configuration works with the chat provider but not realtime, proving a real parity breakage. While count=1, the impact is clearly blocking — users cannot validate tool usage with realtime models, which is a primary use case. The issue author provides concrete reproduction steps (yaml test case) and explicitly identifies it as a configuration/implementation gap in Promptfoo's realtime provider. This is not a feature request — it is a functional regression/lack of implementation for an existing feature (tool calling) on a supported provider.

source_issues.title: Realtime models do not trigger tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Realtime models do not invoke configured tools; returns plain text instead. Same tools.yaml config works with openai:chat provider but fails with openai:realtime provider. Breaks tool-use validation for realtime models.

signals.topic: Pydantic v2 compatibility error blocks Ollama LLM and embedding import entirely
signals.summary: The PydanticUserError on import prevents all Ollama LLM and embedding usage after Pydantic v2 migration.
signals.review_reason: This issue completely blocks all Ollama LLM and embedding usage after Pydantic v2 migration. The error occurs at import time, making the entire Ollama integration unusable for any user on v2. This is a main workflow failure with no workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: PydanticUserError: The `__modify_schema__` method is not supported in Pydantic v2. Use `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` instead in class `SecretStr`.
source_issues.evidence: PydanticUserError thrown on import when using Ollama LLM or embeddings with Pydantic v2, completely blocking the integration.

signals.topic: Async rate limiter uses threading.Lock, blocking asyncio event loop under concurrent load
signals.summary: async_acquire() in TokenBucketRateLimiter and SlidingWindowRateLimiter uses threading.Lock in async context, causing event loop blocking and throughput collapse.
signals.review_reason: Blocks async LLM/embedding pipelines under concurrent load. All coroutines freeze when using rate limiters with the synchronous lock. This is a significant performance degradation and potential throughput collapse for production async pipelines, though it requires concurrent load to manifest.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: [llama-index-core] async_acquire() in TokenBucketRateLimiter and SlidingWindowRateLimiter blocks the asyncio event loop (threading.Lock used in async context)
source_issues.evidence: threading.Lock used inside async methods causes the asyncio event loop to block. Under concurrent async workloads using rate limiters, all coroutines freeze, causing latency spikes and throughput collapse.

signals.topic: vLLM Qwen3 reasoning content silently discarded due to field name mismatch (reasoning vs reasoning_content)

source_issues.evidence: from_openai_message checks for 'reasoning_content' but vLLM returns 'reasoning', silently dropping all reasoning traces. Users assume Qwen3 isn't reasoning when the trace is discarded at the conversion layer. Downstream components (workflows, agents, evaluators) receive empty reasoning.

signals.review_reason: Image download is a key feature of LlamaParse that is completely unavailable. Users cannot integrate extracted images into markdown or downstream pipelines. This blocks a core multimodal document processing workflow.

signals.topic: BM25 retriever IndexNode serialization/deserialization mismatch causes silent data corruption on retrieval
signals.summary: model_dump() replacing dict() broke IndexNode obj serialization; deserialization fails and silently replaces obj with TextNode backup, corrupting data in retrieval pipelines.
signals.review_reason: BM25 retrieval with IndexNodes is a common pattern. The serialization mismatch causes silent data corruption — the obj field content is lost and replaced with a text representation. Users may not notice until downstream components fail unexpectedly.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: obj serialization mismatch
source_issues.evidence: When using BM25 retriever with IndexNodes, the obj field is silently replaced with a backup TextNode containing serialized text instead of the original object. The exception is caught and data is corrupted silently.

signals.review_reason: Three distinct issues blocking plugin ecosystem: ESM export mismatch (#1904), missing npm package affecting 3 plugins (#1903), wrong semver constraints blocking entire plugin store (#1902). count=3 meets P0 threshold but scope is plugin installation ecosystem, not main flow — P1 appropriate. source_issues.title: plugin-agentic-qe@3.0.0-alpha.4 declares peer-deps >=3.0.0 blocking npm install in plugin store
source_issues.evidence: Peer dependencies declare '>=3.0.0' which excludes all alpha versions (semver semantics). No stable 3.0.0 ever published. Anyone with plugin-agentic-qe in plugin store cannot install any other @claude-flow/* plugin. Complete installation tree blockage.

signals.topic: MCP transport closes during tool use, making entire MCP server unusable for rest of session
signals.summary: stdio MCP server writes diagnostics to fd 1, corrupting JSON-RPC framing and causing transport to drop. All subsequent MCP tool calls fail with 'Transport closed' including mcp_status. Affects all Codex/Claude MCP users.
aliases: MCP tools fail with Transport closed
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocked — MCP server becomes completely inoperable mid-session. All tools fail with Transport closed. Two distinct sources confirm this pattern (#1910 direct bug report, #1912 PR fix). No workaround available during active session. Downgraded from P0 to P1 because count=2 (below P0 threshold of count>=3), despite strong user impact.

source_issues.title: bug: claude-flow MCP transport closes during broad tool smoke test
source_issues.evidence: Transport closes during hooks batch; all subsequent MCP tool calls fail with 'Transport closed' including mcp_status. Entire MCP server unusable for rest of active session. All tools in the session become broken.

source_issues.title: stdio MCP server writes diagnostics to fd 1, corrupting JSON-RPC framing
source_issues.evidence: PR #1912 confirms root cause: stdio MCP server writes diagnostics to fd 1, corrupting JSON-RPC framing → client drops transport → every MCP tool fails with Transport closed. MCP unusable for affected users until fix lands.

signals.topic: Stop hook causes ETIMEDOUT errors and unnecessary network downloads on every response
signals.summary: Stop hook runs 'npx claude-flow@alpha' on every assistant response. npx checks npm registry each time, fails with ETIMEDOUT on network interruption. Also references outdated package name causing unnecessary downloads.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation — ETIMEDOUT errors surface to users on every response when network hiccups occur. Unnecessary network requests waste bandwidth. Errors are non-blocking but create user confusion/frustration. Two issues confirm the pattern.

source_issues.title: Stop hook ETIMEDOUT: npx downloads claude-flow@alpha on every response
source_issues.evidence: Stop hook runs 'npx claude-flow@alpha' on every assistant response. npx checks npm registry each time, fails with ETIMEDOUT on any network interruption (VPN reconnect, interface flap). Error surfaces visibly to users on every response. Network waste and UX degradation.

source_issues.title: Stop hook uses outdated package name claude-flow@alpha instead of ruflo
source_issues.evidence: Stop hook references old package name 'claude-flow@alpha'. Every session end triggers npx to attempt downloading old package. Causes unnecessary network requests on every response.

signals.topic: Memory store silently loses all data on process exit (sql.js in-memory backend)
signals.summary: sql.js memory backend does not persist writes. All data is silently lost on process exit. Semantic search finds nothing after restart.
aliases: memory store data loss on restart
signals.review_reason: Critical data loss — users lose ALL memory data on every process exit. Silently fails with no warning. Directly undermines the core memory functionality which is the primary value proposition of the tool. review_reason gives explicit strong evidence: 'Critical — data loss' confirmed by maintainer triage in #1918.

source_issues.title: sql.js memory backend silently loses all data on process exit
source_issues.evidence: sql.js memory backend is in-memory only; without db.save() after writes, memory store silently loses all data on process exit and semantic search finds nothing after restart. Adds flushDb() after all 7 write sites. Critical data loss. Supersedes #1873.

signals.topic: Agent execute fails with 404 due to deprecated model name aliases
signals.summary: All three model aliases (haiku, sonnet, opus) resolve to deprecated Anthropic model names that return HTTP 404. agent_execute cannot function at all.
aliases: deprecated model names causing agent_execute failure
signals.review_reason: Main flow completely blocked — agent_execute fails with 404 errors for all model aliases. Direct execution failure visible to users. count=1 but review_reason provides explicit strong user impact: 'agent_execute cannot function' is a total feature unavailability. P0 warranted by severity despite single-issue count.

source_issues.title: agent_execute fails 404 — model aliases map to deprecated claude-3-* model names
source_issues.evidence: All three model aliases (haiku→claude-3-5-haiku-latest 404, sonnet→claude-3-5-sonnet-latest 404, opus→claude-3-opus-latest 404) resolve to deprecated model names. API key auth is valid (no 401). Main flow completely blocked — agent_execute cannot run any agents.

signals.topic: Session state regression: `navigate` reports success but `get url` returns `about:blank` after navigation
signals.summary: Regression introduced after v0.24.0: `navigate` reports successful navigation (shows correct URL), but `get url` and `screenshot` still return `about:blank`. Session state is not updated after navigation. This silently corrupts AI agent workflows as agents trust the navigate success message.
aliases: Navigation reports success but browser stays on about:blank
Session state not persisting after navigate call
signals.review_reason: P0 regression: confirmed behavioral regression from known-good version (v0.24.0) that silently corrupts session state. AI agents rely on session state being consistent after navigation. The navigate command reporting success while the browser state is not updated is a severe user trap that will cause downstream workflow failures to appear as agent errors rather than tool bugs.

source_issues.title: agent-browser back to `about:blank` after get url or screenshot
source_issues.evidence: User reproduces: navigate reports '✓ Google https://www.google.com/', but get url immediately returns 'about:blank' and screenshot shows blank page. Regression from v0.24.0 confirmed.

source_issues.title: snapshot -s <selector> produces duplicate elements when AX tree contains virtual nodes without backendDOMNodeId
source_issues.evidence: Secondary evidence: session state and AX tree traversal inconsistencies observed in the same release window, both impacting agent workflows that depend on reliable browser state.

signals.topic: Proxy environment variables with trailing slash cause navigation failure (ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES)
signals.summary: When HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY contain a trailing slash (e.g., http://127.0.0.1:7890/), `agent-browser open` fails with ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES because Chromium's --proxy-server flag rejects trailing slashes. This is common in Docker/container environments where proxy configs are set by third-party tools that automatically append trailing slashes.
signals.review_reason: User-impacting workflow failure: navigation command fails with a clear error in common container environments where proxy tools automatically append trailing slashes. This is a main-flow blocking issue that prevents any agent-browser command from accessing remote URLs through a proxy.

source_issues.title: ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES when proxy environment variables contain trailing slash
source_issues.evidence: User reports proxy env vars with trailing slash cause Chromium to fail with net::ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES, blocking browser navigation. Root cause traced to cli/src/native/cdp/chrome.rs line 185 where proxy URL is passed directly without trimming trailing slash.

signals.topic: Windows headed mode (--headed) does not surface browser window when invoked from non-TTY context
signals.summary: On Windows 11, `agent-browser --headed` fails to show a visible browser window when the CLI is invoked from a non-TTY context (e.g., PowerShell -File via bash 2>&1 from WSL/Git Bash). The daemon starts but no window appears. This blocks all browser-mediated auth flows (OIDC PKCE, manual login) for AI agent scripts on Windows.
aliases: Browser window not visible on Windows when invoked from CI/agent context
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking on Windows: --headed is designed for browser-mediated authentication, a core use case. AI agent scripts by definition run in non-TTY contexts (wrapped by a parent harness), making this a direct blocker for the primary intended workflow on Windows 11.

source_issues.title: Windows 11: --headed not surfacing window when invoked from non-TTY context (PowerShell -File via bash 2>&1)
source_issues.evidence: 5-attempt repro shows window appears correctly from interactive TTY pwsh but vanishes when invoked via bash 2>&1. Downstream team documented this as a regression blocking OIDC PKCE mint flows and had to implement a workaround using chrome-devtools-axi instead.

signals.topic: Chrome crashes with 'trap int3' in Docker container environments
signals.summary: Chrome 147.0.7727.57 crashes with a kernel-level 'trap int3' when `agent-browser` runs inside Docker containers (observed on alpine/openclaw base image). Chrome processes dump core, preventing any browser automation in containerized CI/CD environments.
aliases: Chrome process trap int3 in container
signals.review_reason: Main-flow failure in a specific environment: browser commands fail on every invocation in Docker containers, which is a critical blocker for users running agent-browser in containerized CI/CD pipelines. Chrome itself crashes rather than the CLI gracefully handling the environment.

source_issues.title: Chrome 147.0 crashes with "trap int3" when running in docker
source_issues.evidence: Chrome crashes on every `agent-browser open` call inside Docker. Multiple SIGTRAP core dumps captured. User suspects --enable-unsafe-swiftshader flag as potential cause.

signals.topic: AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME environment variable not respected (only --session flag works)
signals.summary: Setting `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME` env var does not restore login state, while passing `--session` with the same value works correctly. Also, the help text lists AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME twice. This breaks users who rely on environment variables for session management configuration.
aliases: Session name env var not working
signals.review_reason: User experience inconsistency: the environment variable API for session management is silently ignored while the --session flag works, forcing users to use CLI flags instead of env vars. This is an observable behavioral bug affecting session persistence workflows, though it does not block the main open/navigate flow.

source_issues.title: Fix that AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME=foo does not work, although passing --session foo works to restore login state
source_issues.evidence: User reports that --session flag correctly restores login state but AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME env var does not. Additionally, help text lists the variable twice. Inconsistent API between CLI flag and env var.

signals.topic: Missing top-level LICENSE file causes downstream vendoring scripts to fail
signals.summary: The repository declares MIT license in README prose but lacks a top-level LICENSE file, causing vendoring/sync scripts of downstream consumers to fail by default and requiring explicit --accept-missing-license-file overrides.
aliases: Missing LICENSE file breaks downstream license compliance tooling
signals.review_reason: Issue #249 demonstrates concrete user impact: downstream consumers' redistribution workflows are actively broken. The sync script fails by default and only recovers with an explicit override flag, making this a real workflow blocker for anyone vendoring the skills into their own projects. The GitHub API returning licenseInfo: null also breaks automated compliance tooling.

source_issues.title: Add a top-level LICENSE file matching the README's MIT declaration
source_issues.evidence: Downstream consumer's vendoring sync script fails by default when LICENSE is absent; must fall back to embedding full MIT text manually and requires --accept-missing-license-file flag override. Compliance/audit tooling and downstream marketplaces look for the file, not README prose.

signals.topic: Broken relative links in react-best-practices/AGENTS.md after rules directory restructuring
signals.summary: Relative links in the AGENTS.md reference rule files that were moved under a rules/ subdirectory, resulting in 404 links that break agent navigation through the skill documentation.
aliases: Broken markdown links in skill documentation after refactoring
signals.review_reason: Issue #254 identifies broken links in a core skill (react-best-practices) that would cause agents consuming the AGENTS.md to encounter 404s when following those references. This degrades the skill's usability, though it does not block the entire agent-skills system from functioning.

source_issues.title: Broken relative links in react-best-practices AGENTS.md
source_issues.evidence: Three specific relative links in skills/react-best-practices/AGENTS.md point to outdated paths (e.g. ./async-defer-await.md instead of ./rules/async-defer-await.md), causing broken navigation when agents or users follow them.

signals.topic: convertToModelMessages sends rawInput string as tool_use.input causing unrecoverable Anthropic 400 in multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: When a tool call has output-error state with rawInput as a string, convertToModelMessages sends that string as tool_use.input. Anthropic requires a dict, returning 400. Since the corrupted message is in history, every retry replays the same invalid message — permanently breaking multi-turn conversations.
signals.review_reason: Single issue, but represents a complete workflow break in multi-turn conversations: once a tool generates invalid JSON and the SDK stores the raw string in message history, the conversation is permanently stuck — every retry hits the same 400. This is a blocking main-flow failure with no graceful degradation. Clear root cause, reproduction steps, and work-around provided.

signals.topic: MCP HTTP/SSE transport does not downgrade mcp-protocol-version header after initialization, breaking servers like Figma Dev Mode
signals.summary: HttpMCPTransport always emits LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION in the mcp-protocol-version header, ignoring the version negotiated during initialize. Servers that only support older versions (e.g., Figma Dev Mode supports up to 2025-06-18 but client sends 2025-11-25) reject all post-init requests with 400. The client init hangs permanently.
signals.review_reason: Real functional break for any MCP server that does not support the absolute latest protocol version. The SDK sends a hardcoded latest version header in all post-init requests, violating the MCP spec. With Figma Dev Mode MCP Server specifically, the client becomes completely unusable — init hangs after the first 400. Has a confirmed fix patch via pnpm patch. Excluded from P0 only because count=1 and is a single-provider edge case.

signals.topic: AI Gateway intermittently throws GatewayTimeoutError, GatewayResponseError, and AbortError under normal production load
signals.summary: Under normal production load (~50-100 concurrent AI calls), @ai-sdk/gateway randomly throws GatewayTimeoutError, GatewayResponseError, and AbortError across all models (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic). Timeouts fire at ~900ms despite 90s timeout config, suggesting gateway itself is dropping connections. Affects both generateText and ToolLoopAgent workflows.
signals.review_reason: Intermittent but real production reliability issue affecting core API calls. Under normal (not extreme) production load, all three error types occur randomly across multiple providers. The provided stress-test reproduction script demonstrates the failures systematically. Excluded from P0 only because intermittent errors may partially be upstream infrastructure, though the ~900ms timeout behavior strongly suggests SDK/gateway-level connection management issues.

signals.topic: ai package hard-pins @opentelemetry/api@1.9.0 causing lost child spans when app uses ^1.9.1
signals.summary: ai@6.0.176 declares @opentelemetry/api as an exact dependency on 1.9.0. When an app uses @opentelemetry/api@1.9.1, two physical copies of the OpenTelemetry API are installed. OpenTelemetry global/context registration is split across versions, causing child spans to disappear while root spans still export. Specifically affects instrumentation that requires active parent spans.
signals.review_reason: Directly breaks OpenTelemetry observability in production applications that update the OTel API to a compatible patch version. Child spans silently disappear while root spans export, making it appear as an exporter issue. Requires manual package-manager override to fix. Only count=1 but user impact is high — observability is a critical production requirement.

signals.topic: Azure OpenAI file upload fails for files larger than 32MB with 'file urls can not be larger than 32 mb' error
signals.summary: When sending file attachments above 32MB to Azure OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini), the SDK throws 'failed to download file: file urls can not be larger than 32 mb'. Files at 30MB work fine. The user cannot find documentation on supported file size limits and has no workaround.
signals.review_reason: User-facing file upload failure at a specific file size threshold. While only count=1, it represents a real missing feature (no clear SDK-side file size limit documentation) and a poor error message. Users uploading PDFs in the 30-50MB range will hit this silently.

signals.topic: Bundled postcss <8.5.10 in next causes npm audit to report moderate XSS findings for end users
signals.summary: Next.js bundles a version of postcss below 8.5.10 (affected by GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 XSS), which causes npm audit to report moderate XSS findings when users install next or @next/third-parties. Users cannot resolve the vulnerability without ignoring the warning.
aliases: postcss XSS vulnerability bundled by next
signals.review_reason: 依赖漏洞导致用户体验损失：虽然 XSS 实际影响范围有限（postcss 在服务器端使用），但 npm audit 报告 moderate 漏洞造成用户焦虑且无法自动解决，阻塞 CI/CD 流程（audit 失败）。4 条独立 issue 确认此问题的持续影响。

source_issues.title: @next/third-parties pins next@16.3.0-canary.14 in devDependencies, which bundles vulnerable postcss <8.5.10 (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93)
source_issues.evidence: Installing @next/third-parties@16.2.5 + next@16.2.5 causes npm audit to report 3 moderate findings for postcss XSS (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93). Users cannot resolve without ignoring audit.

source_issues.title: @next/third-parties pins next@16.3.0-canary.14 in devDependencies, which bundles vulnerable postcss <8.5.10 (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #93604: @next/third-parties bundles postcss below 8.5.10, triggering npm audit.

source_issues.title: @next/third-parties pins next@16.3.0-canary.14 in devDependencies, which bundles vulnerable postcss <8.5.10 (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #93604: same postcss vulnerability triggered by @next/third-parties.

source_issues.title: postcss bundled by next is vulnerable to XSS (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93) — please update to >=8.5.10
source_issues.evidence: next bundles postcss <8.5.10, npm audit reports moderate XSS. Users cannot resolve without ignoring the warning.

signals.topic: Middleware matcher config does not support route groups, forcing overly broad wildcard patterns
signals.summary: Middleware matcher config does not support route groups. matcher: '/(dashboard)/(.*)' does not match routes inside the (dashboard) route group. Users must use overly broad '/:path*' patterns as a workaround, reducing security and precision.
signals.review_reason: 功能缺失导致安全隐患：Middleware 不支持路由组匹配，用户被迫使用过于宽泛的通配符模式 '/:path*'，降低了中间件路由匹配的精确性，增加了误匹配风险。非阻断但影响安全边界。

source_issues.title: Support route groups in Middleware matcher config
source_issues.evidence: Middleware matcher '/(dashboard)/(.*)' does not match routes inside (dashboard) route group. Workaround '/:path*' is too broad and reduces middleware security precision.

source_issues.title: Support route groups in Middleware matcher config
source_issues.evidence: Same as #93723. Route groups in middleware matcher not supported. Duplicate report confirms ongoing user demand.

signals.topic: Server Actions regression: all forms receive empty FormData after 16.2.6 security release upgrade
signals.summary: After upgrading to 16.2.6, every form using useActionState + server actions receives empty FormData {} on the server side despite inputs being present in DOM at submission time. This is a regression introduced by the security patch itself, blocking all form submissions in production.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：所有使用 useActionState 的表单在升级 16.2.6 后全部收不到 FormData 数据，生产环境表单提交通用失败。用户影响明确且无替代方案，属于安全补丁引入的回归性阻断 bug。

source_issues.title: Server Actions receive empty FormData after upgrading to 16.2.6 (security release regression)
source_issues.evidence: ALL forms using useActionState + server action receive empty FormData {} on server. All form inputs present in DOM at submission time. Regression from security patch. Blocks every form submission in production.

signals.topic: Build crashes with SIGTRAP signal when combining Pages Router + i18n + next/font + standalone output
signals.summary: Next.js 16.2.x build crashes with SIGTRAP when building a project with Pages Router, i18n (7 locales), next/font (Noto Sans), output: standalone, and middleware. Upgrading from 16.1.7 to 16.2.5/16.2.6 triggers the crash immediately after creating an optimized production build.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：构建过程在生产打包阶段直接崩溃（SIGTRAP），使用 Pages Router + i18n + next/font + standalone 的项目无法完成构建，无法进行生产部署。退回到 16.1.7 可绕过，但阻碍升级路径。

source_issues.title: Next.js 16.2.x build crash (SIGTRAP) with Pages Router + i18n + next/font + standalone
source_issues.evidence: Build worker exits with SIGTRAP signal on 16.2.5/16.2.6. Affects Pages Router + i18n (7 locales) + next/font (Noto Sans) + output standalone + middleware combination. Blocks all production deployments after upgrade.

signals.topic: 0-byte file permanently corrupts next/image disk-LRU cache, blocking image optimization
signals.summary: A 0-byte file left in .next/cache/images/ (caused by killing next dev mid-write on Windows, OOM, or antivirus interrupt) permanently corrupts the image disk-LRU cache singleton. The cache becomes permanently unusable and cannot be recovered, blocking all image optimization.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用且无自愈能力：图片 LRU 缓存被 0 字节文件永久污染后无法恢复，next/image 的图片优化功能在生产环境彻底失效。用户需手动清理缓存且仍可能在下次遇到同样情况。

source_issues.title: next/image: a single 0-byte file in .next/cache/images/ permanently poisons the disk-LRU singleton
source_issues.evidence: 0-byte file in image cache permanently poisons LRU singleton. Caused by killing next dev mid-write on Windows (Ctrl-C, OOM, antivirus). Cache becomes permanently unusable. Includes repro repo.

signals.topic: npm publish failure blocks SDK version distribution
signals.summary: Latest SDK version 1.19.41 was not published to npm, preventing developers from installing it via npm and blocking their development/deployment workflows. CI build succeeded but npm publish step failed silently.
signals.review_reason: npm publish failure is a real user-impacting issue: developers cannot install the latest SDK version via npm, blocking their development and CI pipelines. The issue provides explicit evidence of the CI run and the missing package on npm, indicating a workflow failure rather than a request.

source_issues.title: Latest npm sdk version not published
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports version 1.19.41 not published to npm, references CI run showing the build succeeded but npm publish did not propagate the package. This blocks any developer trying to `npm install` the latest SDK version.

signals.topic: Turborepo LSP extension fails to start, connect, or function properly in VSCode across multiple failure modes
signals.summary: The Turborepo VSCode extension (turbod-based LSP server) exhibits multiple critical failures: it crashes immediately on startup (Windows), fails to resolve user-configured `turbo.path` in settings, and incorrectly flags transit nodes in turbo.json as non-existent tasks. These issues collectively render the core LSP functionality (schema validation, turbo.json editing) unusable.
signals.review_reason: The Turborepo LSP is a key developer tooling feature, and multiple distinct failure modes (server crash, path resolution broken, false positive error flags, transit node validation failure) collectively make the LSP unusable. With 4 distinct issues spanning multiple months and affecting core IDE integration, this represents a sustained failure of the extension's primary value proposition. The issues are reproducible and have confirmed user impact across Windows and Mac platforms.

source_issues.title: [Turborepo LSP] Fails to connect and start language server
source_issues.evidence: LSP server crashes immediately with 'failed to connect to daemon after 3 retries' and 'Server crashed 5 times in the last 3 minutes'. The turbo daemon connection fails, making the entire LSP feature completely unavailable on Windows. No workaround provided.

source_issues.title: [LSP] Extension fails to resolve turbo.path in VSC
source_issues.evidence: User-configured relative paths for `turbo.path` in .vscode/settings.json are completely ignored. The extension falls back to searching globally, taking multiple attempts. The extension always falls back to global turbo detection even when a local turbo is explicitly configured.

source_issues.title: [VS Code Extension] Transit Nodes gives `turbo:no-such-task` error
source_issues.evidence: Setting a transit node in turbo.json (e.g., topology task in dependsOn) causes the LSP extension to show `turbo:no-such-task` error. The transit node pattern is valid in turbo but the LSP incorrectly validates it as a missing task, causing false error reporting in the editor.

source_issues.title: vscode extension incorrectly flags "$TURBO_EXTENDS$" as deprecated env var
source_issues.evidence: The VSCode extension displays a deprecation error for the `$TURBO_EXTENDS$` variable syntax, incorrectly flagging it as deprecated via codemod warning. This is a false positive that degrades the editing experience and undermines trust in the LSP's validation.

signals.topic: `turbo prune --docker` produces invalid lockfile with Bun, causing Docker builds to fail
signals.summary: When using `turbo prune --docker` with Bun as the package manager, the pruned lockfile contains inconsistent dependency entries (e.g., missing nested npm packages that are still referenced by kept packages), causing `bun install --frozen-lockfile` to fail inside Docker builds. Affects both literal workspace and nested npm package scenarios.
aliases: bun prune frozen lockfile docker fails
signals.review_reason: Multiple reproducible cases (3 issues) all blocking the critical Docker-based CI/CD pipeline for monorepos using Bun. The prune operation is a core turbo feature that produces corrupt output, making the entire monorepo Docker build workflow unusable. Issue #12780 additionally causes silent config corruption via the codemod tool, which is a primary onboarding/maintenance path.

source_issues.title: literal workspaces + `turbo prune --docker` + `bun install` fails
source_issues.evidence: Docker build fails at `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` with 'Workspace not found' errors. Blocks the entire Docker image build pipeline for monorepos using Bun.

source_issues.title: Turbo prune emits invalid Bun lockfile for pruned workspace with nested npm package entries
source_issues.evidence: Pruned bun.lock references `@npmcli/metavuln-calculator` as a dependency but the pruned lockfile drops the matching nested package entry. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` fails inside Docker with 'failed to resolve prod dependency' error. Docker build pipeline blocked.

source_issues.title: schema.json for v2-9-12 is not deployed (404)
source_issues.evidence: The codemod tool (`pnpm dlx @turbo/codemod@latest update`) updates turbo.json to point to a non-existent schema URL (v2-9-12 returns 404), silently producing invalid configurations. Blocks proper schema validation and codemod workflow.

signals.topic: SIGINT signal not forwarded to child processes when `script-shell=sh`, breaking graceful shutdown on Windows in CI
signals.summary: When running turbo tasks with `script-shell=sh` (the default on Windows), SIGINT signals from Ctrl+C are not forwarded to child processes, causing graceful shutdown sequences to never trigger. This is a critical workflow issue for Windows developers and CI environments that rely on proper process termination.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: the SIGINT forwarding failure has no workaround for Windows users who cannot switch to bash (security policy restriction). This blocks graceful shutdown — a critical feature for any long-running process in dev or CI. The issue is actively discussed (2 comments) and marked as recently active with a clear reproduction path.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` is not forwarded properly when `script-shell=sh`
source_issues.evidence: Child process never receives SIGINT when script-shell=sh, resulting in no graceful shutdown sequence executing. The user explicitly notes they cannot switch to bash due to Windows security policy restrictions, meaning there is no workaround for affected users. Blocks clean process termination in dev and CI workflows on Windows.

signals.topic: Turborepo daemon file watcher fails on APFS secondary volumes, blocking daemon startup
signals.summary: The turbo daemon fails to start on certain APFS volumes (particularly case-sensitive secondary/external volumes) with the error 'timed out waiting for initial fsevents cookie: filewatching failed to start'. This blocks the daemon from running at all on affected filesystem configurations, forcing users to run with `--no-daemon` and lose caching benefits.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, the issue causes the turbo daemon (a core performance feature) to be completely unusable on a specific but documented filesystem configuration (APFS secondary volumes). The workaround of `--no-daemon` has significant performance implications (no caching). The issue has been open since 2023 with intermittent activity, suggesting it has not been adequately addressed and may affect users beyond the single reporter who use similar filesystem setups.

source_issues.title: [turborepo] failed to contact turbod/timed out waiting for initial fsevents cookie: filewatching failed to start
source_issues.evidence: Daemon process repeatedly fails to start on APFS case-sensitive secondary volume with 'timed out waiting for initial fsevents cookie' error. The user notes this affects any repo on their secondary partition, and the same repo works on their primary partition. Workaround of `turbo daemon start` fails consistently. Workaround requires using `--no-daemon` flag, losing all caching benefits. Affected filesystem configuration is documented and reproducible.

signals.topic: Terminal escape codes / gibberish characters appear after running `turbo dev` on macOS
signals.summary: After running `turbo dev`, quitting the server, and interacting with the terminal, strange ANSI escape codes appear in the terminal. This creates a degraded developer experience on macOS, particularly when using pnpm as the package manager.
signals.review_reason: This is a UX degradation issue rather than a main flow blocker. While 24 comments suggest user concern, the issue is isolated to macOS with pnpm, appears to have been partially addressed (closed with 'needs: author input'), and the terminal can be reset to recover.
