signals.topic: vercel env add CLI silently stores empty string while reporting success
signals.summary: The `vercel env add` command reports 'Added Environment Variable' with a normal success message, but `vercel env pull` reveals the variable was stored as an empty string. All input patterns (stdin, --value flag, file redirect) reproduce the bug 100% of the time. This is a silent failure — no error signal is emitted despite the variable being incorrect. For secrets (Stripe webhook secrets, HMAC keys, service role tokens), this causes production outages with no visible error until the next signature verification or API call fails.
aliases: vercel env add empty string silent failure
env variable silent empty value bug
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow failure with explicit production impact evidence. The CLI reports success (green message) but silently stores empty string — a classic silent failure pattern that is particularly dangerous for secrets. The author explicitly describes how this can cause production outages for critical integrations (Stripe webhooks, HMAC keys, service role tokens). Count=1 because it is a single reported bug, but the severity is high enough to warrant P1 rather than P0.

source_issues.title: vercel env add reports success but stores empty string (CLI 53.3.2)
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible silent failure: all three input patterns (stdin, --value flag, file redirect) store empty string despite success message. Verified via `od -c` showing DATE = " " \n. Production secrets (Stripe webhook, HMAC keys) can silently become empty strings with a green CLI receipt, causing production outage with no error signal.

signals.topic: vercel logs pagination bug returns duplicate entries when result set exceeds 50
signals.summary: The `vercel logs --since <window> --json --limit N` command returns duplicate log entries once there are more than 50 logs in the time window. The first page (50 records) is fetched correctly; every subsequent page returns the same first page again, duplicating the same 50 entries until --limit is reached. The root cause is server-side: the `/api/logs/?page=N` endpoint appears to ignore the page parameter and returns the first page each time while still reporting `pagination.hasMore: true`.
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow failure that breaks the core use case of the `vercel logs` command. Instead of returning distinct log entries as expected, the CLI returns duplicates, wasting developer time, corrupting debugging data, and making it impossible to reliably search through logs beyond 50 entries. The author provides concrete reproduction steps using `awk` to prove byte-identical duplicates. The root cause is identified as server-side pagination ignoring the page parameter. P1 due to clear user impact on a primary debugging workflow, despite count=1.

source_issues.title: vercel logs returns duplicate entries when there are more than 50 results and --limit > 50
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible: `--limit 100` returns 100 total entries but only 50 unique. `awk '{n++; u[$0]++} END {print 'total:', n; print 'unique:', length(u)}'` shows 'total: 100, unique: 50'. Root cause traced to server-side `/api/logs/?page=N` ignoring page parameter. Reproduced on CLI versions 53.1.0 and 53.3.2.

signals.topic: vercel@53.3.0 depends on unpublished @vercel/elysia@0.1.74, blocking CI/CD installation
signals.summary: The vercel@53.3.0 package declares a dependency on @vercel/elysia@0.1.74 which has never been published to npm (latest available is 0.1.73). This causes pnpm dlx and other package managers to fail during installation with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION`. All CI/CD pipelines that dynamically install the Vercel CLI (e.g., in GitHub Actions with `pnpm dlx vercel@$VERCEL_CLI_VERSION`) are blocked.
signals.review_reason: This is a packaging/release defect that blocks the main deployment automation flow. CI/CD pipelines that install the Vercel CLI via pnpm dlx are completely broken after version 53.3.0. This directly impacts every team using dynamic CLI version installation in their CI workflows. The author provides the exact error message and the fix path. While the issue was resolved quickly, it represents a real deployment-blocking regression in a shipped release.

source_issues.title: vercel@53.3.0 depends on unpublished @vercel/elysia@0.1.74
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly blocks CI/CD pipelines: 'This blocks CI jobs that install the Vercel CLI dynamically with pnpm dlx.' Error message: 'ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION No matching version found for @vercel/elysia@0.1.74. The latest release of @vercel/elysia is "0.1.73".' The issue was closed the same day after the package was presumably published, but the defect existed in a released version.

signals.topic: Skew Protection only injected for edge runtime, not nodejs — feature silently disabled
signals.summary: The @vercel/react-router vite plugin only injects the Vercel entry server (which sets the `__vdpl` Skew Protection cookie) for edge runtime routes. Routes using the default `nodejs` runtime fall back to React Router's built-in `entry.server.node.tsx`, which has no skew protection. After each deploy, clients with cached HTML get 404s for old content-hashed asset chunks. Skew Protection appears enabled in the dashboard but is actually non-functional for nodejs deployments.
signals.review_reason: This is a key feature (Skew Protection) being silently non-functional for the default nodejs runtime. Users who enable the feature in the dashboard get no indication it is broken — they only discover the issue when clients with cached HTML start getting 404s after deploys. The root cause is a one-line guard in the plugin code that restricts injection to edge runtime only. Impact is real (404s on cached assets post-deploy), but count=1 and only affects a specific framework (React Router), so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: @vercel/react-router: Skew Protection entry.server only injected for edge runtime, not nodejs
source_issues.evidence: Verified with `curl -sI <deployment-url>` showing no `Set-Cookie: __vdpl=...` header for nodejs runtime. The `__vdpl` Skew Protection cookie is only set for edge runtime. Confirmed via code inspection: `injectVercelEntryServer` is only called inside `createServerBundles` when `config.runtime === 'edge'`. Users who enable skew protection and deploy with nodejs runtime get a false sense of security — the feature appears enabled but is silently non-functional, causing 404s on cached assets after deploys.

signals.topic: vercel logs lacks historical log support and hangs indefinitely when no new logs
signals.summary: The `vercel logs` command only shows live logs from the current moment and hangs indefinitely when no new logs are being generated. Unlike standard CLI tools (docker logs, kubectl logs), it cannot show historical logs. Users must go to the web dashboard to access historical logs. This breaks expected CLI patterns and prevents AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) from accessing historical logs programmatically.
aliases: vercel logs cannot show historical logs
signals.review_reason: This is a UX degradation affecting the core debugging workflow. The `vercel logs` command hanging indefinitely when no traffic is present is a poor developer experience, and the lack of historical log support forces users to switch to the web dashboard for routine debugging tasks. However, this is a feature gap rather than a blocking bug — the command works when logs are actively being generated. Count=1 and it is a long-standing open feature request, justifying P2 priority.

source_issues.title: Historical logs in `vercel logs` command
source_issues.evidence: The command hangs indefinitely when no traffic: 'waiting for new logs...' with no timeout or historical retrieval. No CLI flag exists for `--since` or `--last` to access past logs. Historical logs only available via web dashboard. Breaks expected developer CLI patterns and blocks AI tool integration (Claude Code, Cursor) from using vercel logs for debugging.
